rules.sourceSeverityText: Avoid use of high risk drugs
rules.summary: CPIC Table 2 classifies dapsone as high risk for acute hemolytic anemia in G6PD deficiency (strong recommendation). For G6PD-deficient patients, CPIC recommends avoiding high-risk drugs.
rules.quote: Dapsone | High | Strong
rules.actionQuote: Avoid use of high risk drugs

rules.sourceSeverityText: No reason to avoid a low-to-no risk drug based on G6PD status at standard doses
rules.summary: CPIC Table 2 classifies ciprofloxacin as low-to-no risk in G6PD deficiency (optional recommendation). There is no reason to avoid it based on G6PD status at standard doses.
rules.quote: Ciprofloxacin | Low-to-no | Optional
rules.actionQuote: No reason to avoid a low-to-no risk drug based on G6PD status at standard doses

rules.sourceSeverityText: No reason to avoid a low-to-no risk drug based on G6PD status at standard doses
rules.summary: CPIC Table 2 classifies hydroxychloroquine as low-to-no risk in G6PD deficiency (moderate recommendation). There is no reason to avoid it based on G6PD status at standard doses.
rules.quote: Hydroxychloroquine | Low-to-no | Moderate
rules.actionQuote: No reason to avoid a low-to-no risk drug based on G6PD status at standard doses

rules.sourceSeverityText: it is recommended to use sulfamethoxazole normally without regard to G6PD status
rules.summary: CPIC Table 2 classifies sulfamethoxazole as low-to-no risk in G6PD deficiency (optional recommendation). CPIC recommends using it normally without regard to G6PD status. The strength is optional because some regulatory agencies advise caution.
rules.quote: Sulfamethoxazole | Low-to-no | Optional
rules.actionQuote: As a low-to-no risk medication, it is recommended to use sulfamethoxazole normally without regard to G6PD status ( Table 5 ), although the strength of the recommendation is “optional,” given that the authors recognize it is the subject of “caution” from some regulatory agencies.

rules.sourceSeverityText: No reason to avoid a low-to-no risk drug based on G6PD status at standard doses

rules.actionQuote: No reason to avoid a low-to-no risk drug based on G6PD status at standard doses

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with: ... hypersensitivity to codeine
rules.summary: Contraindicated in patients with hypersensitivity to codeine (e.g., anaphylaxis).
rules.quote: hypersensitivity to codeine, acetaminophen, or any of the formulation excipients (e.g., anaphylaxis)

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with: ... hypersensitivity to ... acetaminophen
rules.summary: Contraindicated in patients with hypersensitivity to acetaminophen (e.g., anaphylaxis).
rules.quote: hypersensitivity to codeine, acetaminophen, or any of the formulation excipients (e.g., anaphylaxis)

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with
rules.summary: Contraindicated in patients with significant respiratory depression.
rules.quote: Acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets are contraindicated in patients with: significant respiratory depression

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with
rules.summary: Contraindicated in patients with acute or severe bronchial asthma in an unmonitored setting or in the absence of resuscitative equipment.
rules.quote: acute or severe bronchial asthma in an unmonitored setting or in the absence of resuscitative equipment

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with
rules.summary: Contraindicated in patients with known or suspected gastrointestinal obstruction, including paralytic ileus.
rules.quote: known or suspected gastrointestinal obstruction, including paralytic ileus

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated for: All children younger than 12 years of age
rules.summary: Applies to children younger than 12 years only: contraindicated because of life-threatening respiratory depression and death.
rules.quote: Acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets are contraindicated for: All children younger than 12 years of age

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated for: ... Post-operative management in children younger than 18 years of age following tonsillectomy and/or adenoidectomy
rules.summary: Contraindicated for post-operative management in children younger than 18 years after tonsillectomy and/or adenoidectomy.
rules.quote: Post-operative management in children younger than 18 years of age following tonsillectomy and/or adenoidectomy

rules.sourceSeverityText: Avoid the use ... in adolescents 12 to 18 years of age who have other risk factors
rules.summary: Applies to adolescents 12 to 18 years with other risk factors for sensitivity to respiratory depression: avoid unless benefits outweigh risks.
rules.quote: Avoid the use of acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets in adolescents 12 to 18 years of age who have other risk factors that may increase their sensitivity to the respiratory depressant effects of codeine unless the benefits outweigh the risks.

rules.sourceSeverityText: use caution when selecting a dosage for an elderly patient
rules.summary: Elderly patients may have increased sensitivity; use caution in dose selection, usually starting low, titrate slowly and frequently reevaluate for CNS depression.
rules.quote: Elderly patients (aged 65 years or older) may have increased sensitivity to acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets. In general, use caution when selecting a dosage for an elderly patient, usually starting at the low end of the dosing range
rules.actionQuote: Titrate the dosage of acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets slowly in geriatric patients and frequently reevaluate the patient for signs of central nervous system depression

rules.sourceSeverityText: should not use
rules.summary: CYP2D6 ultra-rapid metabolizers convert codeine to morphine more rapidly and may have life-threatening respiratory depression even at labeled doses; they should not use this product.
rules.quote: Therefore, individuals who are ultra-rapid metabolizers should not use acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets.

rules.sourceSeverityText: should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus
rules.summary: Pregnancy Category C: no adequate studies in pregnant women; use only if the potential benefit justifies the fetal risk.
rules.quote: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.

rules.sourceSeverityText: can result in withdrawal in the neonate
rules.summary: Extended use during pregnancy can cause neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome, which may be life-threatening; observe newborns and ensure treatment is available.
rules.quote: Use of acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets for an extended period of time during pregnancy can result in withdrawal in the neonate.
rules.actionQuote: Advise pregnant women using opioids for an extended period of time of the risk of neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome and ensure that appropriate treatment will be available

rules.sourceSeverityText: are not recommended for use in pregnant women during or immediately prior to labor
rules.summary: Not recommended during or immediately before labor, when other analgesic techniques are more appropriate.
rules.quote: Acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets are not recommended for use in pregnant women during or immediately prior to labor, when other analgesic techniques are more appropriate.

rules.sourceSeverityText: breastfeeding is not recommended
rules.summary: Because of possible excess sedation, respiratory depression and death in a breastfed infant, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment.
rules.quote: Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, including excess sedation, respiratory depression, and death in a breastfed infant, advise patients that breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets

rules.sourceSeverityText: The risk of acute liver failure is higher
rules.summary: The risk of acetaminophen-associated acute liver failure is higher in individuals with underlying liver disease.
rules.quote: The risk of acute liver failure is higher in individuals with underlying liver disease and in individuals who ingest alcohol while taking acetaminophen.

rules.sourceSeverityText: The risk of acute liver failure is higher
rules.summary: The risk of acetaminophen-associated acute liver failure is higher in individuals who ingest alcohol while taking acetaminophen.
rules.quote: The risk of acute liver failure is higher in individuals with underlying liver disease and in individuals who ingest alcohol while taking acetaminophen.

rules.sourceSeverityText: the risk of adverse reactions to this drug may be greater
rules.summary: These drugs are substantially excreted by the kidney and the risk of adverse reactions may be greater in impaired renal function.
rules.quote: These drugs are known to be substantially excreted by the kidney, and the risk of adverse reactions to this drug may be greater in patients with impaired renal function.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Regularly evaluate patients with a history of seizure disorders
rules.summary: Codeine may increase seizure frequency in seizure disorders; regularly evaluate for worsened seizure control.
rules.quote: The codeine in acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets may increase the frequency of seizures in patients with seizure disorders, and may increase the risk of seizures occurring in other clinical settings associated with seizures. Regularly evaluate patients with a history of seizure disorders for worsened seizure control during acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets therapy.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Risks are increased
rules.summary: Risks of addiction, abuse and misuse are increased with a personal or family history of substance abuse or mental illness.
rules.quote: Risks are increased in patients with a personal or family history of substance abuse (including drug or alcohol abuse or addiction) or mental illness (e.g., major depression).

rules.sourceSeverityText: Regularly evaluate patients
rules.summary: Patients with significant COPD or cor pulmonale, decreased respiratory reserve, hypoxia, hypercapnia or pre-existing respiratory depression are at increased risk of decreased respiratory drive including apnea; regularly evaluate, especially at initiation and titration.
rules.quote: Acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets-treated patients with significant chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or cor pulmonale, and those with a substantially decreased respiratory reserve, hypoxia, hypercapnia, or pre-existing respiratory depression are at increased risk of decreased respiratory drive including apnea, even at recommended dosages of acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets
rules.actionQuote: Regularly evaluate patients, particularly when initiating and titrating acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets and when acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets are given concomitantly with other drugs that depress respiration

rules.sourceSeverityText: Avoid the use
rules.summary: May cause vasodilatation that further reduces cardiac output and blood pressure in circulatory shock; avoid.
rules.quote: Avoid the use of acetaminophen and codeine with circulatory shock.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Avoid the use
rules.summary: Avoid in patients with impaired consciousness or coma.
rules.quote: Avoid the use of acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets in patients with impaired consciousness or coma.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Monitor such patients for signs of sedation and respiratory depression
rules.summary: With increased intracranial pressure or brain tumors, CO2 retention may further raise intracranial pressure; monitor for sedation and respiratory depression, especially at initiation.
rules.quote: Monitor such patients for signs of sedation and respiratory depression, particularly when initiating therapy with acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Regularly evaluate
rules.summary: May cause sphincter of Oddi spasm; regularly evaluate patients with biliary tract disease, including acute pancreatitis, for worsening symptoms.
rules.quote: Regularly evaluate patients with biliary tract disease, including acute pancreatitis, for worsening symptoms.

rules.sourceSeverityText: may cause allergic-type reactions
rules.summary: The tablets contain sodium metabisulfite, which may cause allergic-type reactions including anaphylactic symptoms and asthmatic episodes in susceptible people.
rules.quote: Acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets contain sodium metabisulfite, a sulfite that may cause allergic-type reactions including anaphylactic symptoms and life-threatening or less severe asthmatic episodes in certain susceptible people.

rules.sourceSeverityText: not to use more than one product that contains acetaminophen
rules.summary: Patients should check labels for acetaminophen (APAP) and not use another acetaminophen-containing product with this one.
rules.quote: Instruct patients to look for acetaminophen or APAP on package labels and not to use more than one product that contains acetaminophen.

rules.sourceSeverityText: frequently evaluate the patient
rules.summary: Concomitant serotonergic drugs such as tramadol have caused serotonin syndrome with opioids; if use is warranted, evaluate frequently and stop immediately if serotonin syndrome is suspected..
rules.quote: Serotonergic Drugs The concomitant use of opioids with other drugs that affect the serotonergic neurotransmitter system has resulted in serotonin syndrome. Examples of these drugs include, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs), tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), triptans, 5-HT3 receptor antagonists, drugs that effect the serotonin neurotransmitter system (e.g., mirtazapine, trazodone, tramadol)
rules.actionQuote: If concomitant use is warranted, frequently evaluate the patient, particularly during treatment initiation and dose adjustment. Discontinue acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets immediately if serotonin syndrome is suspected.

rules.sourceSeverityText: frequently evaluate the patient
rules.summary: Concomitant SSRIs have caused serotonin syndrome with opioids; if use is warranted, evaluate frequently and stop immediately if serotonin syndrome is suspected.
rules.quote: Serotonergic Drugs The concomitant use of opioids with other drugs that affect the serotonergic neurotransmitter system has resulted in serotonin syndrome. Examples of these drugs include, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs), tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), triptans, 5-HT3 receptor antagonists, drugs that effect the serotonin neurotransmitter system (e.g., mirtazapine, trazodone, tramadol)
rules.actionQuote: If concomitant use is warranted, frequently evaluate the patient, particularly during treatment initiation and dose adjustment. Discontinue acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets immediately if serotonin syndrome is suspected.

rules.sourceSeverityText: frequently evaluate the patient
rules.summary: Concomitant serotonergic drugs have caused serotonin syndrome with opioids; if use is warranted, evaluate frequently and stop immediately if serotonin syndrome is suspected.
rules.quote: Serotonergic Drugs The concomitant use of opioids with other drugs that affect the serotonergic neurotransmitter system has resulted in serotonin syndrome. Examples of these drugs include, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs), tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), triptans, 5-HT3 receptor antagonists, drugs that effect the serotonin neurotransmitter system (e.g., mirtazapine, trazodone, tramadol)
rules.actionQuote: If concomitant use is warranted, frequently evaluate the patient, particularly during treatment initiation and dose adjustment. Discontinue acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets immediately if serotonin syndrome is suspected.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Reserve concomitant prescribing of these drugs for use in patients for whom alternative treatment options are inadequate
rules.summary: Other opioids (CNS depressants) add to the risk of hypotension, respiratory depression, profound sedation, coma and death; reserve co-prescribing for patients without adequate alternatives and limit doses and durations.
rules.quote: Due to additive pharmacologic effect, the concomitant use of benzodiazepines or other CNS depressants, including alcohol, other sedatives/hypnotics, anxiolytics, tranquilizers, muscle relaxants, general anesthetics, antipsychotics and other opioids, can increase the risk of hypotension, respiratory depression, profound sedation, coma, and death. Reserve concomitant prescribing of these drugs for use in patients for whom alternative treatment options are inadequate.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Evaluate patients at frequent intervals for respiratory depression and sedation
rules.summary: CYP3A4 inhibitors such as macrolide antibiotics may raise codeine and then morphine levels, which may cause fatal respiratory depression; consider dose reduction and evaluate frequently for respiratory depression and sedation.
rules.quote: The concomitant use of acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets and CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as macrolide antibiotics (e.g., erythromycin), azole-antifungal agents (e.g., ketoconazole), and protease inhibitors (e.g., ritonavir), may result in an increase in codeine plasma concentrations, with subsequently greater metabolism by cytochrome CYP2D6, resulting in greater morphine levels, which could increase or prolong adverse reactions and may cause potentially fatal respiratory depression
rules.actionQuote: If concomitant use of CYP3A4 inhibitor is necessary, consider dosage reduction of acetaminophen and codeine tablets until stable drug effects are achieved. Evaluate patients at frequent intervals for respiratory depression and sedation.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Evaluate patients at frequent intervals for respiratory depression and sedation
rules.summary: CYP3A4 inhibitors may raise codeine and then morphine levels, which may cause fatal respiratory depression; consider dose reduction and evaluate frequently for respiratory depression and sedation.
rules.quote: The concomitant use of acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets and CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as macrolide antibiotics (e.g., erythromycin), azole-antifungal agents (e.g., ketoconazole), and protease inhibitors (e.g., ritonavir), may result in an increase in codeine plasma concentrations, with subsequently greater metabolism by cytochrome CYP2D6, resulting in greater morphine levels, which could increase or prolong adverse reactions and may cause potentially fatal respiratory depression
rules.actionQuote: If concomitant use of CYP3A4 inhibitor is necessary, consider dosage reduction of acetaminophen and codeine tablets until stable drug effects are achieved. Evaluate patients at frequent intervals for respiratory depression and sedation.

rules.sourceSeverityText: consider dosage adjustment ... and evaluate patients at frequent intervals
rules.summary: CYP2D6 inhibitors can raise codeine levels but lower morphine levels, which can reduce pain relief or cause opioid withdrawal; stopping the inhibitor can raise morphine levels. Consider dose adjustment and evaluate patients at frequent intervals.
rules.quote: The concomitant use of acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets and CYP2D6 inhibitors (e.g., paroxetine, fluoxetine, bupropion, quinidine) can increase the plasma concentration of codeine, but can decrease the plasma concentration of active metabolite morphine, which could result in reduced analgesic efficacy or symptoms of opioid withdrawal, particularly when an inhibitor is added after a stable dose of acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets are achieved
rules.actionQuote: If concomitant use with a CYP2D6 inhibitor is necessary, or if a CYP2D6 inhibitor is discontinued after concomitant use, consider dosage adjustment of acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets and evaluate patients at frequent intervals.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Evaluate patients at frequent intervals for respiratory depression and sedation
rules.summary: CYP3A4 inhibitors may raise codeine and then morphine levels, which may cause fatal respiratory depression; consider dose reduction and evaluate frequently for respiratory depression and sedation.
rules.quote: The concomitant use of acetaminophen and codeine phosphate tablets and CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as macrolide antibiotics (e.g., erythromycin), azole-antifungal agents (e.g., ketoconazole), and protease inhibitors (e.g., ritonavir), may result in an increase in codeine plasma concentrations, with subsequently greater metabolism by cytochrome CYP2D6, resulting in greater morphine levels, which could increase or prolong adverse reactions and may cause potentially fatal respiratory depression
rules.actionQuote: If concomitant use of CYP3A4 inhibitor is necessary, consider dosage reduction of acetaminophen and codeine tablets until stable drug effects are achieved. Evaluate patients at frequent intervals for respiratory depression and sedation.

rules.sourceSeverityText: evaluate patients for signs of diminished diuresis and/or effects on blood pressure
rules.summary: Opioids can reduce the effect of diuretics. Evaluate for reduced urine output and blood pressure effects, and increase the diuretic dose as needed.
rules.quote: Diuretics Opioids can reduce the efficacy of diuretics by inducing the release of antidiuretic hormone. If concomitant use is warranted evaluate patients for signs of diminished diuresis and/or effects on blood pressure and increase the dosage of the diuretic as needed.
rules.actionQuote: If concomitant use is warranted evaluate patients for signs of diminished diuresis and/or effects on blood pressure and increase the dosage of the diuretic as needed.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Ask a doctor or pharmacist before use
rules.summary: Ask a doctor or pharmacist before using acetaminophen if taking the blood thinning drug warfarin.
rules.quote: Ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if the user is taking the blood thinning drug warfarin

rules.sourceSeverityText: Do not use
rules.summary: Do not use with any other prescription or nonprescription drug containing acetaminophen.
rules.quote: Do not use with any other drug containing acetaminophen (prescription or nonprescription).
rules.actionQuote: If you are not sure whether a drug contains acetaminophen, ask a doctor or pharmacist.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Ask a doctor before use
rules.summary: Ask a doctor before use if the user has liver disease.
rules.quote: Ask a doctor before use if the user has liver disease

rules.sourceSeverityText: Severe liver damage may occur
rules.summary: Severe liver damage may occur if an adult has 3 or more alcoholic drinks every day while using this product.
rules.quote: Severe liver damage may occur if adult takes more than 4,000 mg of acetaminophen in 24 hours child takes more than 5 doses in 24 hours, which is the maximum daily amount taken with other drugs containing acetaminophen adult has 3 or more alcoholic drinks every day while using this product

rules.sourceSeverityText: ask a health professional before use
rules.summary: If pregnant, ask a health professional before use.
rules.quote: If pregnant or breast-feeding, ask a health professional before use.

rules.sourceSeverityText: ask a health professional before use
rules.summary: If breast-feeding, ask a health professional before use.
rules.quote: If pregnant or breast-feeding, ask a health professional before use.

rules.sourceSeverityText: do not take more than 5 tablets in 24 hours
rules.summary: Children 6 to under 12 years: 1 tablet every 4 to 6 hours, no more than 5 tablets in 24 hours, and no more than 5 days unless directed by a doctor.
rules.quote: children 6 years to under 12 years take 1 tablet every 4 to 6 hours while symptoms last do not take more than 5 tablets in 24 hours do not use for more than 5 days unless directed by a doctor

rules.sourceSeverityText: ask a doctor
rules.summary: For children under 6 years, ask a doctor.
rules.quote: children under 6 years ask a doctor

rules.sourceSeverityText: Do not use
rules.summary: Do not use if allergic to acetaminophen or any of the inactive ingredients in this product.
rules.quote: if you are allergic to acetaminophen or any of the inactive ingredients in this product

rules.sourceSeverityText: Limit the dose of simvastatin in patients on amlodipine to 20 mg daily
rules.summary: Amlodipine increases simvastatin exposure. Limit simvastatin to 20 mg daily in patients on amlodipine.
rules.quote: Co-administration of simvastatin with amlodipine increases the systemic exposure of simvastatin. Limit the dose of simvastatin in patients on amlodipine to 20 mg daily
rules.actionQuote: Limit the dose of simvastatin in patients on amlodipine to 20 mg daily

rules.sourceSeverityText: Monitor for hypotension
rules.summary: Monitor for hypotension when sildenafil is given with amlodipine.
rules.quote: Monitor for hypotension when sildenafil is co-administered with amlodipine
rules.actionQuote: Monitor for hypotension when sildenafil is co-administered with amlodipine

rules.sourceSeverityText: Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema when amlodipine is co-administered with CYP3A inhibitors
rules.summary: Strong CYP3A inhibitors such as clarithromycin may increase amlodipine plasma concentrations. The label says to monitor for hypotension and edema with CYP3A inhibitors to judge the need for dose adjustment.
rules.quote: However, strong inhibitors of CYP3A (e.g., itraconazole, clarithromycin) may increase the plasma concentrations of amlodipine to a greater extent
rules.actionQuote: Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema when amlodipine is co-administered with CYP3A inhibitors to determine the need for dose adjustment

rules.sourceSeverityText: may require dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema
rules.summary: Moderate and strong CYP3A inhibitors increase amlodipine exposure and may require dose reduction. Monitor for hypotension and edema to judge the need for dose adjustment.
rules.quote: Co-administration with CYP3A inhibitors (moderate and strong) results in increased systemic exposure to amlodipine and may require dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema when amlodipine is co-administered with CYP3A inhibitors to determine the need for dose adjustment
rules.actionQuote: Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema when amlodipine is co-administered with CYP3A inhibitors to determine the need for dose adjustment

rules.sourceSeverityText: does not affect the exposure to atorvastatin
rules.summary: Co-administered amlodipine does not affect atorvastatin exposure.
rules.quote: Co-administered amlodipine does not affect the exposure to atorvastatin, digoxin, ethanol and the warfarin prothrombin response time.

rules.sourceSeverityText: does not affect the exposure to atorvastatin, digoxin, ethanol and the warfarin prothrombin response time
rules.summary: Co-administered amlodipine does not affect the warfarin prothrombin response time.
rules.quote: Co-administered amlodipine does not affect the exposure to atorvastatin, digoxin, ethanol and the warfarin prothrombin response time.

rules.sourceSeverityText: have no impact on the exposure to amlodipine
rules.summary: Magnesium- and aluminum hydroxide antacids have no impact on amlodipine exposure.
rules.quote: Co-administered cimetidine, magnesium-and aluminum hydroxide antacids, sildenafil, and grapefruit juice have no impact on the exposure to amlodipine.

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated
rules.summary: Amlodipine is contraindicated in patients with known sensitivity to amlodipine.
rules.quote: Amlodipine besylate tablets are contraindicated in patients with known sensitivity to amlodipine.

rules.sourceSeverityText: may be started on 2.5 mg once daily
rules.summary: Patients with hepatic insufficiency (as well as small, fragile or elderly patients) may be started on amlodipine 2.5 mg once daily.
rules.quote: Small, fragile, or elderly patients, or patients with hepatic insufficiency may be started on 2.5 mg once daily

rules.sourceSeverityText: titrate slowly
rules.summary: Amlodipine is extensively metabolized by the liver and its half-life is 56 hours in hepatic impairment; titrate slowly in severe hepatic impairment.
rules.quote: Because amlodipine is extensively metabolized by the liver and the plasma elimination half‑life (t 1/2 ) is 56 hours in patients with impaired hepatic function, titrate slowly when administering amlodipine besylate tablets to patients with severe hepatic impairment.
rules.actionQuote: titrate slowly when administering amlodipine besylate tablets to patients with severe hepatic impairment

rules.sourceSeverityText: a lower initial dose may be required
rules.summary: Elderly patients have decreased amlodipine clearance with about 40-60% higher AUC, and a lower initial dose may be required.
rules.quote: Elderly patients have decreased clearance of amlodipine with a resulting increase of AUC of approximately 40–60%, and a lower initial dose may be required

rules.sourceSeverityText: is not known
rules.summary: Amlodipine 2.5 to 5 mg daily lowers blood pressure in patients 6 to 17 years; its effect in children under 6 is not known.
rules.quote: Amlodipine besylate tablets (2.5 to 5 mg daily) are effective in lowering blood pressure in patients 6 to 17 years [ see Clinical Studies (14.1) ] . Effect of amlodipine on blood pressure in patients less than 6 years of age is not known.

rules.sourceSeverityText: are not sufficient to inform a drug-associated risk
rules.summary: Limited post-marketing data in pregnancy are not sufficient to inform a drug-associated risk of major birth defects or miscarriage. Poorly controlled hypertension in pregnancy carries risks to mother and fetus.
rules.quote: The limited available data based on post-marketing reports with amlodipine besylate use in pregnant women are not sufficient to inform a drug-associated risk for major birth defects and miscarriage. There are risks to the mother and fetus associated with poorly controlled hypertension in pregnancy

rules.sourceSeverityText: No adverse effects of amlodipine on the breastfed infant have been observed
rules.summary: Amlodipine is present in human milk at a median relative infant dose of 4.2%; no adverse effects on the breastfed infant have been observed. Effects on milk production are unknown.
rules.quote: Limited available data from a published clinical lactation study reports that amlodipine is present in human milk at an estimated median relative infant dose of 4.2%. No adverse effects of amlodipine on the breastfed infant have been observed. There is no available information on the effects of amlodipine on milk production.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Symptomatic hypotension is possible
rules.summary: Symptomatic hypotension is possible with amlodipine, particularly in severe aortic stenosis; acute hypotension is unlikely because of gradual onset.
rules.quote: Symptomatic hypotension is possible, particularly in patients with severe aortic stenosis. Because of the gradual onset of action, acute hypotension is unlikely.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Worsening angina and acute myocardial infarction can develop
rules.summary: Worsening angina and acute myocardial infarction can develop after starting or increasing amlodipine, particularly in severe obstructive coronary artery disease.
rules.quote: Worsening angina and acute myocardial infarction can develop after starting or increasing the dose of amlodipine besylate tablets, particularly in patients with severe obstructive coronary artery disease.

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity reactions
rules.summary: Contraindicated after a serious hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome) to amoxicillin.
rules.quote: Amoxicillin and Clavulanate Potassium Extended Release Tablets is contraindicated in patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity reactions (e.g., anaphylaxis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome) to amoxicillin, clavulanate or to other beta-lactam antibacterial drugs (e.g., penicillins and cephalosporins).

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity reactions
rules.summary: Contraindicated after a serious hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome) to clavulanate.
rules.quote: Amoxicillin and Clavulanate Potassium Extended Release Tablets is contraindicated in patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity reactions (e.g., anaphylaxis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome) to amoxicillin, clavulanate or to other beta-lactam antibacterial drugs (e.g., penicillins and cephalosporins).

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity reactions
rules.summary: Contraindicated after a serious hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome) to other beta-lactam antibacterial drugs.
rules.quote: Amoxicillin and Clavulanate Potassium Extended Release Tablets is contraindicated in patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity reactions (e.g., anaphylaxis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome) to amoxicillin, clavulanate or to other beta-lactam antibacterial drugs (e.g., penicillins and cephalosporins).

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity reactions
rules.summary: Contraindicated after a serious hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome) to penicillins.
rules.quote: Amoxicillin and Clavulanate Potassium Extended Release Tablets is contraindicated in patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity reactions (e.g., anaphylaxis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome) to amoxicillin, clavulanate or to other beta-lactam antibacterial drugs (e.g., penicillins and cephalosporins).

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity reactions
rules.summary: Contraindicated after a serious hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome) to cephalosporins.
rules.quote: Amoxicillin and Clavulanate Potassium Extended Release Tablets is contraindicated in patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity reactions (e.g., anaphylaxis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome) to amoxicillin, clavulanate or to other beta-lactam antibacterial drugs (e.g., penicillins and cephalosporins).

rules.sourceSeverityText: more likely to occur in individuals with a history of penicillin hypersensitivity
rules.summary: Serious anaphylactic reactions are more likely with a history of penicillin hypersensitivity; the label asks for careful inquiry about prior reactions to penicillins before starting.
rules.quote: These reactions are more likely to occur in individuals with a history of penicillin hypersensitivity and/or a history of sensitivity to multiple allergens.
rules.actionQuote: Before initiating therapy with Amoxicillin and Clavulanate Potassium Extended Release Tablets, careful inquiry should be made regarding previous hypersensitivity reactions to penicillins, cephalosporins, or other allergens.

rules.sourceSeverityText: careful inquiry should be made regarding previous hypersensitivity reactions
rules.summary: Before starting, the label asks for careful inquiry about previous hypersensitivity reactions to cephalosporins.
rules.quote: Before initiating therapy with Amoxicillin and Clavulanate Potassium Extended Release Tablets, careful inquiry should be made regarding previous hypersensitivity reactions to penicillins, cephalosporins, or other allergens.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Appropriate monitoring should be undertaken
rules.summary: Abnormal prolongation of prothrombin time (increased INR) has been reported with amoxicillin and oral anticoagulants. Monitoring is advised and anticoagulant dose adjustment may be necessary.
rules.quote: Abnormal prolongation of prothrombin time (increased international normalized ratio [INR]) has been reported in patients receiving amoxicillin and oral anticoagulants. Appropriate monitoring should be undertaken when anticoagulants are prescribed concurrently.
rules.actionQuote: Adjustments in the dose of oral anticoagulants may be necessary to maintain the desired level of anticoagulation.

rules.sourceSeverityText: is contraindicated
rules.summary: Contraindicated in patients with a previous history of cholestatic jaundice/hepatic dysfunction associated with amoxicillin/clavulanate treatment.
rules.quote: Amoxicillin and Clavulanate Potassium Extended Release Tablets is contraindicated in patients with a previous history of cholestatic jaundice/hepatic dysfunction associated with treatment with amoxicillin/clavulanate potassium.

rules.sourceSeverityText: is contraindicated
rules.summary: This extended-release product is contraindicated with creatinine clearance less than 30 mL/min and in hemodialysis patients.
rules.quote: Amoxicillin and Clavulanate Potassium Extended Release Tablets is contraindicated in patients with severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance less than 30 mL/min) and in hemodialysis patients.

rules.sourceSeverityText: have not been studied in patients with renal impairment
rules.summary: The pharmacokinetics of this product have not been studied in renal impairment (it is contraindicated below CrCl 30 mL/min).
rules.quote: The pharmacokinetics of Amoxicillin and Clavulanate Potassium Extended Release Tablets have not been studied in patients with renal impairment.

rules.sourceSeverityText: should be dosed with caution and hepatic function monitored at regular intervals
rules.summary: In hepatic impairment, dose with caution and monitor hepatic function at regular intervals.
rules.quote: Hepatically impaired patients should be dosed with caution and hepatic function monitored at regular intervals

rules.sourceSeverityText: Avoid ... use in patients with mononucleosis
rules.summary: A high percentage of patients with mononucleosis who receive amoxicillin develop an erythematous rash; avoid use in mononucleosis.
rules.quote: A high percentage of patients with mononucleosis who receive amoxicillin develop an erythematous skin rash. Avoid Amoxicillin and Clavulanate Potassium Extended Release Tablets use in patients with mononucleosis.

rules.sourceSeverityText: have not established a drug-associated risk
rules.summary: Decades of epidemiologic and pharmacovigilance data have not established a drug-associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal outcomes.
rules.quote: Available data from published epidemiologic studies and pharmacovigilance case reports over several decades of use with amoxicillin and clavulanate during pregnancy have not established a drug-associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal outcomes.

rules.sourceSeverityText: may be associated with an increased risk of necrotizing enterocolitis in neonates
rules.summary: In women with preterm prelabor rupture of membranes, prophylactic amoxicillin/clavulanate may be associated with an increased risk of neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis.
rules.quote: A study in women with preterm prelabor rupture of membranes (PPROM) reported that prophylactic treatment with amoxicillin and clavulanate may be associated with an increased risk of necrotizing enterocolitis in neonates

rules.sourceSeverityText: should be monitored for these symptoms
rules.summary: Amoxicillin is present in human milk; diarrhea, irritability and rash have been reported in exposed infants, who should be monitored for these symptoms.
rules.quote: There are reports of diarrhea, irritability, and rash in infants exposed to amoxicillin and clavulanate through breast milk; therefore, infants exposed to Amoxicillin and Clavulanate Potassium Extended Release Tablets should be monitored for these symptoms.

rules.sourceSeverityText: have been established for pediatric patients weighing greater than or equal to 40 kg who are able to swallow tablets
rules.summary: Safety and effectiveness of this extended-release product are established only for pediatric patients weighing at least 40 kg who can swallow tablets; they receive the adult dose.
rules.quote: The safety and effectiveness of Amoxicillin and Clavulanate Potassium Extended Release Tablets have been established for pediatric patients weighing greater than or equal to 40 kg who are able to swallow tablets.

rules.sourceSeverityText: it may be useful to monitor renal function
rules.summary: Elderly patients are more likely to have decreased renal function, so monitoring renal function may be useful.
rules.quote: Because elderly patients are more likely to have decreased renal function, it may be useful to monitor renal function.

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients who have experienced a serious hypersensitivity reaction
rules.summary: Amoxicillin is contraindicated after a serious hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome) to amoxicillin.
rules.quote: AMOXIL is contraindicated in patients who have experienced a serious hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome) to AMOXIL or to other β-lactam antibacterial drugs (e.g., penicillins and cephalosporins).

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients who have experienced a serious hypersensitivity reaction
rules.summary: Amoxicillin is contraindicated after a serious hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome) to other beta-lactam antibacterial drugs.
rules.quote: AMOXIL is contraindicated in patients who have experienced a serious hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome) to AMOXIL or to other β-lactam antibacterial drugs (e.g., penicillins and cephalosporins).

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients who have experienced a serious hypersensitivity reaction
rules.summary: Amoxicillin is contraindicated after a serious hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome) to penicillins.
rules.quote: AMOXIL is contraindicated in patients who have experienced a serious hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome) to AMOXIL or to other β-lactam antibacterial drugs (e.g., penicillins and cephalosporins).

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients who have experienced a serious hypersensitivity reaction
rules.summary: Amoxicillin is contraindicated after a serious hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome) to cephalosporins.
rules.quote: AMOXIL is contraindicated in patients who have experienced a serious hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome) to AMOXIL or to other β-lactam antibacterial drugs (e.g., penicillins and cephalosporins).

rules.sourceSeverityText: more likely to occur in individuals with a history of penicillin hypersensitivity
rules.summary: Serious anaphylactic reactions are more likely in people with a history of penicillin hypersensitivity; the label asks for careful inquiry about prior reactions to penicillins before starting.
rules.quote: These reactions are more likely to occur in individuals with a history of penicillin hypersensitivity and/or a history of sensitivity to multiple allergens.
rules.actionQuote: Before initiating therapy with amoxicillin, careful inquiry should be made regarding previous hypersensitivity reactions to penicillins, cephalosporins, or other allergens.

rules.sourceSeverityText: careful inquiry should be made regarding previous hypersensitivity reactions
rules.summary: Before starting amoxicillin, the label asks for careful inquiry about previous hypersensitivity reactions to cephalosporins.
rules.quote: Before initiating therapy with amoxicillin, careful inquiry should be made regarding previous hypersensitivity reactions to penicillins, cephalosporins, or other allergens.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Appropriate monitoring should be undertaken
rules.summary: Abnormal prolongation of prothrombin time (increased INR) has been reported with amoxicillin and oral anticoagulants. Monitoring is advised and anticoagulant dose adjustment may be necessary.
rules.quote: Abnormal prolongation of prothrombin time (increased international normalized ratio [INR]) has been reported in patients receiving amoxicillin and oral anticoagulants. Appropriate monitoring should be undertaken when anticoagulants are prescribed concurrently.
rules.actionQuote: Adjustments in the dose of oral anticoagulants may be necessary to maintain the desired level of anticoagulation.

rules.sourceSeverityText: may interfere with the bactericidal effects of penicillin ... clinical significance of this interaction is not well documented
rules.summary: Macrolides may interfere with the bactericidal effects of penicillin in vitro; the clinical significance is not well documented.
rules.quote: Chloramphenicol, macrolides, sulfonamides, and tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal effects of penicillin. This has been demonstrated in vitro ; however, the clinical significance of this interaction is not well documented.

rules.sourceSeverityText: may interfere with the bactericidal effects of penicillin ... clinical significance of this interaction is not well documented
rules.summary: Sulfonamides may interfere with the bactericidal effects of penicillin in vitro; the clinical significance is not well documented.
rules.quote: Chloramphenicol, macrolides, sulfonamides, and tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal effects of penicillin. This has been demonstrated in vitro ; however, the clinical significance of this interaction is not well documented.

rules.sourceSeverityText: should be used during pregnancy only if clearly needed
rules.summary: Pregnancy Category B: no fetal harm in animal studies, but no adequate human studies; use in pregnancy only if clearly needed.
rules.quote: There was no evidence of harm to the fetus due to amoxicillin. There are, however, no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Because animal reproduction studies are not always predictive of human response, amoxicillin should be used during pregnancy only if clearly needed.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Caution should be exercised
rules.summary: Penicillins are excreted in human milk and amoxicillin may sensitize infants; use caution in nursing women.
rules.quote: Penicillins have been shown to be excreted in human milk. Amoxicillin use by nursing mothers may lead to sensitization of infants. Caution should be exercised when amoxicillin is administered to a nursing woman.

rules.sourceSeverityText: do not generally require a reduction in dose unless the impairment is severe
rules.summary: Patients with impaired renal function do not generally need a dose reduction unless the impairment is severe.
rules.quote: Patients with impaired renal function do not generally require a reduction in dose unless the impairment is severe.

rules.sourceSeverityText: should NOT receive the 875 mg dose
rules.summary: Patients with GFR less than 30 mL/min should not receive the 875 mg dose; reduced regimens are given for severe renal impairment.
rules.quote: Renal impairment patients with a glomerular filtration rate of less than 30 mL/min should NOT receive the 875 mg dose.

rules.sourceSeverityText: 500 mg or 250 mg every 12 hours
rules.summary: For GFR 10 to 30 mL/min the regimen is 500 mg or 250 mg every 12 hours, depending on infection severity.
rules.quote: GFR 10 to 30 mL/min 500 mg or 250 mg every 12 hours, depending on the severity of the infection

rules.sourceSeverityText: 500 mg or 250 mg every 24 hours
rules.summary: For GFR less than 10 mL/min or hemodialysis the regimen is 500 mg or 250 mg every 24 hours; on hemodialysis an additional dose is given during and at the end of dialysis.
rules.quote: GFR less than 10 mL/min 500 mg or 250 mg every 24 hours, depending on severity of the infection Hemodialysis 500 mg or 250 mg every 24 hours, depending on severity of the infection Administer an additional dose both during and at the end of dialysis

rules.sourceSeverityText: should not be administered to patients with mononucleosis
rules.summary: A high percentage of patients with mononucleosis who receive amoxicillin develop an erythematous rash; it should not be given to them.
rules.quote: A high percentage of patients with mononucleosis who receive amoxicillin develop an erythematous skin rash. Thus, amoxicillin should not be administered to patients with mononucleosis.

rules.sourceSeverityText: chewable tablets contain aspartame which contains phenylalanine
rules.summary: Amoxicillin chewable tablets contain aspartame (phenylalanine); the oral suspension does not contain phenylalanine and can be used by phenylketonurics. Applies to the chewable formulation only.
rules.quote: The oral suspension formulations of Amoxicillin do not contain phenylalanine and can be used by phenylketonurics.

rules.sourceSeverityText: the recommended upper dose of amoxicillin is 30 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours
rules.summary: Applies only to infants younger than 12 weeks (3 months): because of immature renal function, the upper dose is 30 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours.
rules.quote: Due to incompletely developed renal function affecting elimination of amoxicillin in this age group, the recommended upper dose of amoxicillin is 30 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours.

rules.sourceSeverityText: care should be taken in dose selection, and it may be useful to monitor renal function
rules.summary: Elderly patients are more likely to have decreased renal function, so care should be taken in dose selection and renal function monitoring may be useful.
rules.quote: Because elderly patients are more likely to have decreased renal function, care should be taken in dose selection, and it may be useful to monitor renal function.

rules.sourceSeverityText: do not exceed atorvastatin calcium 20 mg
rules.summary: Macrolide antibiotics such as clarithromycin significantly increase atorvastatin levels. In patients taking clarithromycin, atorvastatin should not exceed 20 mg, and patients should be monitored for myopathy.
rules.quote: Atorvastatin plasma levels were significantly increased with concomitant administration of atorvastatin calcium with select azole antifungals or macrolide antibiotics, due to inhibition of CYP3A4 and/or transporters [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )]. Intervention: In patients taking clarithromycin or itraconazole, do not exceed atorvastatin calcium 20 mg
rules.actionQuote: In patients taking clarithromycin or itraconazole, do not exceed atorvastatin calcium 20 mg

rules.sourceSeverityText: listed under 4 CONTRAINDICATIONS: Hypersensitivity to atorvastatin or any excipients in atorvastatin calcium
rules.summary: Hypersensitivity to atorvastatin or any excipient is a contraindication; anaphylaxis, angioneurotic edema, erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis have been reported.
rules.quote: Hypersensitivity to atorvastatin or any excipients in atorvastatin calcium. Hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, angioneurotic edema, erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated
rules.summary: Atorvastatin is contraindicated in acute liver failure.
rules.quote: Atorvastatin calcium is contraindicated in patients with acute liver failure or decompensated cirrhosis

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated
rules.summary: Atorvastatin is contraindicated in decompensated cirrhosis.
rules.quote: Atorvastatin calcium is contraindicated in patients with acute liver failure or decompensated cirrhosis

rules.sourceSeverityText: may be at increased risk for hepatic injury
rules.summary: Patients with a history of liver disease may be at increased risk of hepatic injury with atorvastatin. Liver enzyme testing is considered before starting and when clinically indicated.
rules.quote: Patients who consume substantial quantities of alcohol and/or have a history of liver disease may be at increased risk for hepatic injury [see Use in Specific Populations ( 8.7 )]. Consider liver enzyme testing before atorvastatin calcium initiation and when clinically indicated thereafter.

rules.sourceSeverityText: plasma concentrations of atorvastatin calcium are markedly increased
rules.summary: In chronic alcoholic liver disease atorvastatin concentrations are markedly increased: about 4-fold in Child-Pugh A and about 11- to 16-fold in Child-Pugh B. The label gives no dose instruction for this.
rules.quote: In patients with chronic alcoholic liver disease, plasma concentrations of atorvastatin calcium are markedly increased. C max and AUC are each 4-fold greater in patients with Childs-Pugh A disease. C max and AUC are approximately 16-fold and 11-fold increased, respectively, in patients with Childs-Pugh B disease.

rules.sourceSeverityText: may be at increased risk for hepatic injury
rules.summary: Patients who consume substantial quantities of alcohol may be at increased risk of hepatic injury with atorvastatin.
rules.quote: Patients who consume substantial quantities of alcohol and/or have a history of liver disease may be at increased risk for hepatic injury

rules.sourceSeverityText: Monitor all patients with renal impairment for development of myopathy
rules.summary: Renal impairment is a risk factor for myopathy and rhabdomyolysis; monitor all patients with renal impairment for myopathy.
rules.quote: Renal impairment is a risk factor for myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. Monitor all patients with renal impairment for development of myopathy.
rules.actionQuote: Monitor all patients with renal impairment for development of myopathy.

rules.sourceSeverityText: there is no dosage adjustment in patients with renal impairment
rules.summary: Renal impairment does not affect atorvastatin plasma concentrations, so no dose adjustment is needed.
rules.quote: Renal impairment does not affect the plasma concentrations of atorvastatin calcium, therefore there is no dosage adjustment in patients with renal impairment

rules.sourceSeverityText: Discontinue atorvastatin calcium when pregnancy is recognized. Alternatively, consider the ongoing therapeutic needs of the individual patient.
rules.summary: Atorvastatin may cause fetal harm based on its mechanism of action. The label says to discontinue it when pregnancy is recognized, or alternatively to consider the patient's ongoing therapeutic needs.
rules.quote: Discontinue atorvastatin calcium when pregnancy is recognized. Alternatively, consider the ongoing therapeutic needs of the individual patient. Atorvastatin calcium decreases synthesis of cholesterol and possibly other biologically active substances derived from cholesterol; therefore, atorvastatin calcium may cause fetal harm when administered to pregnant patients based on the mechanism of action
rules.actionQuote: Discontinue atorvastatin calcium when pregnancy is recognized.

rules.sourceSeverityText: breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with atorvastatin calcium
rules.summary: Because of potential serious adverse reactions in a breastfed infant, breastfeeding is not recommended during atorvastatin treatment.
rules.quote: Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed infant, based on the mechanism of action, advise patients that breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with atorvastatin calcium

rules.sourceSeverityText: Monitor geriatric patients receiving atorvastatin calcium for the increased risk of myopathy
rules.summary: Age 65 or over is a risk factor for atorvastatin-associated myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. Dose selection should be cautious and geriatric patients monitored for myopathy.
rules.quote: Advanced age (≥65 years) is a risk factor for atorvastatin calcium-associated myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. Dose selection for an elderly patient should be cautious, recognizing the greater frequency of decreased hepatic, renal, or cardiac function, and of concomitant disease or other drug therapy and the higher risk of myopathy. Monitor geriatric patients receiving atorvastatin calcium for the increased risk of myopathy
rules.actionQuote: Monitor geriatric patients receiving atorvastatin calcium for the increased risk of myopathy

rules.sourceSeverityText: have not been established
rules.summary: Safety and effectiveness are established in children 10 years and older with HeFH or HoFH, but not in children younger than 10 or in children with other types of hyperlipidemia.
rules.quote: The safety and effectiveness of atorvastatin calcium have not been established in pediatric patients younger than 10 years of age with HeFH or HoFH, or in pediatric patients with other types of hyperlipidemia (other than HeFH or HoFH).

rules.sourceSeverityText: Risk factors for myopathy include
rules.summary: Uncontrolled hypothyroidism is listed as a risk factor for myopathy with atorvastatin.
rules.quote: Risk factors for myopathy include age 65 years or greater, uncontrolled hypothyroidism, renal impairment, concomitant use with certain other drugs (including other lipid-lowering therapies), and higher atorvastatin calcium dosage

rules.sourceSeverityText: Consider the risk/benefit of use of atorvastatin calcium tablets 80 mg
rules.summary: A higher incidence of hemorrhagic stroke was seen with atorvastatin 80 mg in patients with a recent stroke or TIA. The label says to consider the risk/benefit of the 80 mg dose in patients with recent hemorrhagic stroke.
rules.quote: Consider the risk/benefit of use of atorvastatin calcium tablets 80 mg in patients with recent hemorrhagic stroke.

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in persons with a history of hypersensitivity
rules.summary: Contraindicated with a history of hypersensitivity to ciprofloxacin or any product component.
rules.quote: CIPRO is contraindicated in persons with a history of hypersensitivity to ciprofloxacin, any member of the quinolone class of antibacterials, or any of the product components

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in persons with a history of hypersensitivity
rules.summary: Contraindicated with a history of hypersensitivity to any member of the quinolone class of antibacterials.
rules.quote: CIPRO is contraindicated in persons with a history of hypersensitivity to ciprofloxacin, any member of the quinolone class of antibacterials, or any of the product components

rules.sourceSeverityText: Avoid CIPRO in patients with known history of myasthenia gravis
rules.summary: Fluoroquinolones including ciprofloxacin may exacerbate muscle weakness in myasthenia gravis; avoid in patients with a known history of myasthenia gravis.
rules.quote: Fluoroquinolones, including CIPRO, may exacerbate muscle weakness in patients with myasthenia gravis. Avoid CIPRO in patients with known history of myasthenia gravis .

rules.sourceSeverityText: Avoid fluoroquinolones, including CIPRO
rules.summary: Avoid in patients with a history of tendon disorders or who have had tendinitis or tendon rupture.
rules.quote: Avoid fluoroquinolones, including CIPRO, in patients who have a history of tendon disorders or have experienced tendinitis or tendon rupture

rules.sourceSeverityText: Avoid fluoroquinolones, including CIPRO
rules.summary: Avoid in patients who have previously experienced peripheral neuropathy.
rules.quote: Avoid fluoroquinolones, including CIPRO, in patients who have previously experienced peripheral neuropathy

rules.sourceSeverityText: use CIPRO with caution in epileptic patients
rules.summary: Use with caution in epilepsy and CNS disorders predisposing to seizures.
rules.quote: As with all fluoroquinolones, use CIPRO with caution in epileptic patients and patients with known or suspected CNS disorders that may predispose to seizures or lower the seizure threshold

rules.sourceSeverityText: Avoid CIPRO in patients with known prolongation of the QT interval
rules.summary: Avoid in patients with known QT prolongation or risk factors for QT prolongation or torsade de pointes.
rules.quote: Avoid CIPRO in patients with known prolongation of the QT interval, risk factors for QT prolongation or torsade de pointes (for example, congenital long QT syndrome, uncorrected electrolyte imbalance, such as hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia and cardiac disease, such as heart failure, myocardial infarction, or bradycardia), and patients receiving Class IA antiarrhythmic agents (quinidine, procainamide), or Class III antiarrhythmic agents (amiodarone, sotalol), tricyclic antidepressants, macrolides, and antipsychotics.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Avoid CIPRO in patients with ... risk factors for QT prolongation or torsade de pointes (for example, ... heart failure
rules.summary: Heart failure is listed as a risk factor for QT prolongation or torsade de pointes, in which ciprofloxacin should be avoided.
rules.quote: Avoid CIPRO in patients with known prolongation of the QT interval, risk factors for QT prolongation or torsade de pointes (for example, congenital long QT syndrome, uncorrected electrolyte imbalance, such as hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia and cardiac disease, such as heart failure, myocardial infarction, or bradycardia), and patients receiving Class IA antiarrhythmic agents (quinidine, procainamide), or Class III antiarrhythmic agents (amiodarone, sotalol), tricyclic antidepressants, macrolides, and antipsychotics.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Avoid use in patients with ... hypokalemia
rules.summary: Avoid in patients with hypokalemia (uncorrected electrolyte imbalance is a QT risk factor).
rules.quote: Avoid use in patients with known prolongation, those with hypokalemia, and with other drugs that prolong the QT interval.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Avoid CIPRO in patients with ... uncorrected electrolyte imbalance, such as hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia
rules.summary: Uncorrected hypomagnesemia is listed as a QT/torsade risk factor in which ciprofloxacin should be avoided.
rules.quote: Avoid CIPRO in patients with known prolongation of the QT interval, risk factors for QT prolongation or torsade de pointes (for example, congenital long QT syndrome, uncorrected electrolyte imbalance, such as hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia and cardiac disease, such as heart failure, myocardial infarction, or bradycardia), and patients receiving Class IA antiarrhythmic agents (quinidine, procainamide), or Class III antiarrhythmic agents (amiodarone, sotalol), tricyclic antidepressants, macrolides, and antipsychotics.

rules.sourceSeverityText: reserve CIPRO for use only when there are no alternative antibacterial treatments available
rules.summary: Fluoroquinolone use is followed by an increased rate of aortic aneurysm and dissection; in patients with known aortic aneurysm or at greater risk, reserve ciprofloxacin for when no alternative is available.
rules.quote: In patients with a known aortic aneurysm or patients who are at greater risk for aortic aneurysms, reserve CIPRO for use only when there are no alternative antibacterial treatments available.

rules.sourceSeverityText: careful monitoring of blood glucose is recommended
rules.summary: Blood glucose disturbances (hyper- and hypoglycemia) occur usually in diabetic patients on oral hypoglycemics or insulin; careful blood glucose monitoring is recommended.
rules.quote: Fluoroquinolones, including CIPRO, have been associated with disturbances of blood glucose, including symptomatic hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia, usually in diabetic patients receiving concomitant treatment with an oral hypoglycemic agent (for example, glyburide) or with insulin. In these patients, careful monitoring of blood glucose is recommended.

rules.sourceSeverityText: The risk ... is increased
rules.summary: The risk of fluoroquinolone-associated tendinitis and tendon rupture is increased in patients with kidney, heart or lung transplants (also over 60 years and with corticosteroids).
rules.quote: The risk of developing fluoroquinolone-associated tendinitis and tendon rupture is increased in patients over 60 years of age, in patients taking corticosteroid drugs, and in patients with kidney, heart or lung transplants.

rules.sourceSeverityText: 250–500 mg every 12 hours
rules.summary: Adults with creatinine clearance 30 to 50 mL/min: 250 to 500 mg every 12 hours.
rules.quote: 30–50 250–500 mg every 12 hours

rules.sourceSeverityText: 250–500 mg every 18 hours
rules.summary: Adults with creatinine clearance 5 to 29 mL/min: 250 to 500 mg every 18 hours.
rules.quote: 5–29 250–500 mg every 18 hours

rules.sourceSeverityText: 250–500 mg every 24 hours (after dialysis)
rules.summary: Patients on hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis: 250 to 500 mg every 24 hours, after dialysis.
rules.quote: Patients on hemodialysis or Peritoneal dialysis 250–500 mg every 24 hours (after dialysis)

rules.sourceSeverityText: No information is available on dosing adjustments
rules.summary: Applies to pediatric patients only: no information is available on dose adjustment for moderate to severe renal insufficiency (CrCl < 50 mL/min/1.73 m2).
rules.quote: No information is available on dosing adjustments necessary for pediatric patients with moderate to severe renal insufficiency (that is, creatinine clearance of < 50 mL/min/1.73m 2 ).

rules.sourceSeverityText: no significant changes in ciprofloxacin pharmacokinetics have been observed ... have not been studied
rules.summary: In stable chronic liver cirrhosis no significant pharmacokinetic changes were seen in preliminary studies; acute hepatic insufficiency has not been studied.
rules.quote: In preliminary studies in patients with stable chronic liver cirrhosis, no significant changes in ciprofloxacin pharmacokinetics have been observed. The pharmacokinetics of ciprofloxacin in patients with acute hepatic insufficiency, have not been studied.

rules.sourceSeverityText: have not identified any drug-associated risk
rules.summary: Decades of published experience have not identified a drug-associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes.
rules.quote: Prolonged experience with ciprofloxacin in pregnant women over several decades, based on available published information from case reports, case control studies and observational studies on ciprofloxacin administered during pregnancy, have not identified any drug-associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes

rules.sourceSeverityText: Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment
rules.summary: Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment; a lactating woman may pump and discard milk during treatment and for 2 days after the last dose. For inhalational anthrax, weigh risks and benefits of continuing breastfeeding.
rules.quote: Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment, but a lactating woman may pump and discard breastmilk during treatment and an additional 2 days after the last dose. In patients treated for inhalational anthrax (post exposure), consider the risks and benefits of continuing breastfeeding.

rules.sourceSeverityText: not a drug of first choice in the pediatric population
rules.summary: Not a drug of first choice in children because of an increased incidence of adverse reactions, compared to controls.
rules.quote: Although effective in clinical trials, CIPRO is not a drug of first choice in the pediatric population due to an increased incidence of adverse reactions compared to controls.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Caution should be used when prescribing CIPRO to elderly patients
rules.summary: Elderly patients are at increased risk of severe tendon disorders, further increased with corticosteroids; use caution, especially with corticosteroids.
rules.quote: Geriatric patients are at increased risk for developing severe tendon disorders including tendon rupture when being treated with a fluoroquinolone such as CIPRO. This risk is further increased in patients receiving concomitant corticosteroid therapy.
rules.actionQuote: Caution should be used when prescribing CIPRO to elderly patients especially those on corticosteroids.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Monitor prothrombin time and INR frequently
rules.summary: Ciprofloxacin may increase the anticoagulant effect; monitor prothrombin time and INR frequently during and shortly after co-administration with an oral anticoagulant such as warfarin.
rules.quote: Monitor prothrombin time and INR frequently during and shortly after co-administration of CIPRO with an oral anti-coagulant (for example, warfarin).

rules.sourceSeverityText: Use with caution ... carefully monitor patients under methotrexate therapy
rules.summary: Ciprofloxacin may inhibit methotrexate renal tubular transport and raise methotrexate levels and toxicity risk; carefully monitor patients on methotrexate.
rules.quote: Methotrexate Use with caution Inhibition of methotrexate renal tubular transport potentially leading to increased methotrexate plasma levels Potential increase in the risk of methotrexate associated toxic reactions. Therefore, carefully monitor patients under methotrexate therapy when concomitant CIPRO therapy is indicated.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Use with caution ... Monitor for sildenafil toxicity
rules.summary: Ciprofloxacin causes a two-fold increase in sildenafil exposure; monitor for sildenafil toxicity.
rules.quote: Sildenafil Use with caution Two-fold increase in exposure Monitor for sildenafil toxicity

rules.sourceSeverityText: Use with caution
rules.summary: NSAIDs (but not aspirin) combined with very high doses of quinolones have provoked convulsions in pre-clinical studies and postmarketing; use with caution.
rules.quote: NSAIDs Use with caution Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (but not acetyl salicylic acid) in combination of very high doses of quinolones have been shown to provoke convulsions in pre-clinical studies and in postmarketing.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Drugs Known to Prolong QT Interval Avoid Use
rules.summary: Ciprofloxacin may further prolong the QT interval in patients receiving QT-prolonging drugs, including macrolides; avoid use.
rules.quote: Drugs Known to Prolong QT Interval Avoid Use CIPRO may further prolong the QT interval in patients receiving drugs known to prolong the QT interval (for example, class IA or III antiarrhythmics, tricyclic antidepressants, macrolides, antipsychotics)

rules.sourceSeverityText: Administer CIPRO at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after
rules.summary: Magnesium/aluminum antacids and other multivalent cation products decrease ciprofloxacin absorption; take ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after them.
rules.quote: Administer CIPRO at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium/aluminum antacids; polymeric phosphate binders (for example, sevelamer, lanthanum carbonate) or sucralfate; Videx ® (didanosine) chewable/buffered tablets or pediatric powder for oral solution; other highly buffered drugs; or other products containing calcium, iron or zinc.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Administer CIPRO at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after
rules.summary: Products containing calcium decrease ciprofloxacin absorption; take ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after them.
rules.quote: Administer CIPRO at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium/aluminum antacids; polymeric phosphate binders (for example, sevelamer, lanthanum carbonate) or sucralfate; Videx ® (didanosine) chewable/buffered tablets or pediatric powder for oral solution; other highly buffered drugs; or other products containing calcium, iron or zinc.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Administer CIPRO at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after
rules.summary: Products containing iron decrease ciprofloxacin absorption; take ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after them.
rules.quote: Administer CIPRO at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium/aluminum antacids; polymeric phosphate binders (for example, sevelamer, lanthanum carbonate) or sucralfate; Videx ® (didanosine) chewable/buffered tablets or pediatric powder for oral solution; other highly buffered drugs; or other products containing calcium, iron or zinc.

rules.sourceSeverityText: CIPRO should be taken at least two hours before or six hours after
rules.summary: Antacids, sucralfate, multivitamins and other multivalent cation products decrease ciprofloxacin absorption; take ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after them.
rules.quote: CIPRO should be taken at least two hours before or six hours after Multivalent cation-containing products administration

rules.sourceSeverityText: Avoid Use
rules.summary: Ciprofloxacin may further prolong the QT interval in patients receiving drugs known to prolong the QT interval. Avoid use.
rules.quote: Drugs Known to Prolong QT Interval Avoid Use CIPRO may further prolong the QT interval in patients receiving drugs known to prolong the QT interval (for example, class IA or III antiarrhythmics, tricyclic antidepressants, macrolides, antipsychotics)

rules.sourceSeverityText: Use with caution ... Monitor blood glucose
rules.summary: Severe hypoglycemia, sometimes fatal, has been reported when ciprofloxacin was given with oral antidiabetic agents, mainly sulfonylureas. Monitor blood glucose when they are used together.
rules.quote: Oral antidiabetic drugs Use with caution Glucose-lowering effect potentiated Hypoglycemia sometimes severe has been reported when CIPRO and oral antidiabetic agents, mainly sulfonylureas (for example, glyburide, glimepiride), were co-administered, presumably by intensifying the action of the oral antidiabetic agent. Fatalities have been reported . Monitor blood glucose when CIPRO is co-administered with oral antidiabetic drugs
rules.actionQuote: Monitor blood glucose when CIPRO is co-administered with oral antidiabetic drugs

rules.sourceSeverityText: Concomitant use of clarithromycin with lovastatin or simvastatin is contraindicated
rules.summary: Clarithromycin with simvastatin is contraindicated because clarithromycin increases simvastatin levels and the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. If clarithromycin cannot be avoided, simvastatin must be suspended during treatment.
rules.quote: Concomitant use of clarithromycin with lovastatin or simvastatin is contraindicated [see Contraindications (4.5) ] as these statins are extensively metabolized by CYP3A4, and concomitant treatment with clarithromycin increases their plasma concentration, which increases the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis.
rules.actionQuote: If treatment with clarithromycin cannot be avoided, therapy with lovastatin or simvastatin must be suspended during the course of treatment.

rules.sourceSeverityText: atorvastatin dose should not exceed 20 mg daily
rules.summary: Use caution when prescribing clarithromycin with atorvastatin. If the combination cannot be avoided, atorvastatin should not exceed 20 mg daily.
rules.quote: Exercise caution when prescribing clarithromycin with atorvastatin or pravastatin. In situations where the concomitant use of clarithromycin with atorvastatin or pravastatin cannot be avoided, atorvastatin dose should not exceed 20 mg daily and pravastatin dose should not exceed 40 mg daily.
rules.actionQuote: In situations where the concomitant use of clarithromycin with atorvastatin or pravastatin cannot be avoided, atorvastatin dose should not exceed 20 mg daily

rules.sourceSeverityText: Monitor INR and prothrombin times frequently
rules.summary: Clarithromycin with warfarin carries a risk of serious hemorrhage and significant INR and prothrombin time elevations. Monitor INR and prothrombin time frequently.
rules.quote: There is a risk of serious hemorrhage and significant elevations in INR and prothrombin time when clarithromycin is co-administered with warfarin. Monitor INR and prothrombin times frequently while patients are receiving clarithromycin and oral anticoagulants concurrently
rules.actionQuote: Monitor INR and prothrombin times frequently while patients are receiving clarithromycin and oral anticoagulants concurrently

rules.sourceSeverityText: Serious adverse reactions have been reported (Table 8: Calcium Channel Blockers ... Use With Caution)
rules.summary: Serious adverse reactions, including hypotension and acute kidney injury, have been reported with clarithromycin and CYP3A4-metabolized calcium channel blockers such as amlodipine. Most acute kidney injury reports involved patients 65 or older.
rules.quote: Serious adverse reactions have been reported in patients taking clarithromycin concomitantly with CYP3A4 substrates. These include colchicine toxicity with colchicine; markedly increased transaminases with lomitapide; rhabdomyolysis with simvastatin, lovastatin, and atorvastatin; hypoglycemia and cardiac arrhythmias (e.g., torsades de pointes ) with disopyramide; and hypotension and acute kidney injury with calcium channel blockers metabolized by CYP3A4 (e.g., verapamil, amlodipine, diltiazem, nifedipine). Most reports of acute kidney injury with calcium channel blockers metabolized by CYP3A4 involved elderly patients 65 years of age or older.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Co-administration of these phosphodiesterase inhibitors with clarithromycin is not recommended
rules.summary: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A and increases exposure to sildenafil. Co-administration is not recommended; the label also says dose reduction of the phosphodiesterase inhibitor should be considered.
rules.quote: Co-administration of clarithromycin with sildenafil, tadalafil, or vardenafil will result in increased exposure of these phosphodiesterase inhibitors. Co-administration of these phosphodiesterase inhibitors with clarithromycin is not recommended. Increased systemic exposure of these drugs may occur with clarithromycin; reduction of dosage for phosphodiesterase inhibitors should be considered (see their respective prescribing information).

rules.sourceSeverityText: No Dose Adjustment
rules.summary: Clarithromycin increases omeprazole exposure (gastric pH 5.2 alone vs 5.7 with clarithromycin); the table lists no dose adjustment.
rules.quote: Proton Pump Inhibitors: Omeprazole No Dose Adjustment Omeprazole : The mean 24-hour gastric pH value was 5.2 when omeprazole was administered alone and 5.7 when coadministered with clarithromycin as a result of increased omeprazole exposures

rules.sourceSeverityText: Use With Caution
rules.summary: Omeprazole increases clarithromycin concentrations in gastric tissue and mucus; the table lists this as use with caution.
rules.quote: Proton Pump Inhibitors: Omeprazole Use With Caution Omeprazole : Clarithromycin concentrations in the gastric tissue and mucus were also increased by concomitant administration of omeprazole

rules.sourceSeverityText: Use With Caution
rules.summary: St John's wort is listed among other drugs metabolized by CYP3A with reported CYP3A-based interactions with clarithromycin; use with caution.
