rules.sourceSeverityText: breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with ZOCOR
rules.summary: Because of potential serious adverse reactions in a breastfed infant, breastfeeding is not recommended during simvastatin treatment.
rules.quote: Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed infant, based on the mechanism of action, advise patients that breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with ZOCOR

rules.sourceSeverityText: Monitor geriatric patients receiving ZOCOR for the increased risk of myopathy
rules.summary: Age 65 or over is a risk factor for simvastatin-associated myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. Dose selection should be cautious and geriatric patients monitored for myopathy.
rules.quote: Advanced age (≥65 years) is a risk factor for ZOCOR-associated myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. Dose selection for an elderly patient should be cautious, recognizing the greater frequency of decreased hepatic, renal, or cardiac function, and of concomitant disease or other drug therapy and the higher risk of myopathy. Monitor geriatric patients receiving ZOCOR for the increased risk of myopathy
rules.actionQuote: Monitor geriatric patients receiving ZOCOR for the increased risk of myopathy

rules.sourceSeverityText: have not been established
rules.summary: Safety and effectiveness are established in pediatric patients 10 years and older with HeFH, but not in children younger than 10 with HeFH or in children with other types of hyperlipidemia.
rules.quote: The safety and effectiveness of ZOCOR have not been established in pediatric patients younger than 10 years of age with HeFH or in pediatric patients with other types of hyperlipidemia (other than HeFH).

rules.sourceSeverityText: Risk factors for myopathy include
rules.summary: Uncontrolled hypothyroidism is listed as a risk factor for myopathy with simvastatin.
rules.quote: Risk factors for myopathy include age 65 years or greater, uncontrolled hypothyroidism, renal impairment, concomitant use with certain other drugs (including other lipid-lowering therapies), and higher ZOCOR dosage

rules.sourceSeverityText: Monitor serum potassium within 1 week of initiation or titration
rules.summary: Spironolactone can cause hyperkalemia, and concomitant potassium supplementation or potassium-containing salt substitutes increase the risk. Monitor serum potassium within 1 week of starting or titrating and regularly thereafter.
rules.quote: Spironolactone oral suspension can cause hyperkalemia. This risk is increased by impaired renal function or concomitant potassium supplementation, potassium-containing salt substitutes or drugs that increase potassium, such as angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers [see Drug Interactions ( 7.1 )] . Monitor serum potassium within 1 week of initiation or titration of spironolactone oral suspension and regularly thereafter.
rules.actionQuote: If hyperkalemia occurs, decrease the dose or discontinue spironolactone oral suspension and treat hyperkalemia.

rules.sourceSeverityText: In general, discontinue potassium supplementation in heart failure patients who start spironolactone oral suspension
rules.summary: Potassium supplementation with spironolactone may lead to severe hyperkalemia. In heart failure patients starting spironolactone, potassium supplementation should in general be discontinued.
rules.quote: Concomitant administration of spironolactone oral suspension with potassium supplementation or drugs that can increase potassium may lead to severe hyperkalemia. In general, discontinue potassium supplementation in heart failure patients who start spironolactone oral suspension
rules.actionQuote: In general, discontinue potassium supplementation in heart failure patients who start spironolactone oral suspension

rules.sourceSeverityText: Monitor serum potassium within 1 week of initiation or titration
rules.summary: Potassium supplementation and potassium-containing salt substitutes increase the risk of hyperkalemia with spironolactone. Monitor serum potassium within 1 week of starting or titrating and regularly thereafter.
rules.quote: This risk is increased by impaired renal function or concomitant potassium supplementation, potassium-containing salt substitutes or drugs that increase potassium, such as angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers [see Drug Interactions ( 7.1 )] . Monitor serum potassium within 1 week of initiation or titration of spironolactone oral suspension and regularly thereafter.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Check serum potassium levels when ACE inhibitor or ARB therapy is altered
rules.summary: ACE inhibitors can increase potassium and, with spironolactone, may lead to severe hyperkalemia. Check serum potassium when ACE inhibitor therapy is changed.
rules.quote: Concomitant administration of spironolactone oral suspension with potassium supplementation or drugs that can increase potassium may lead to severe hyperkalemia. In general, discontinue potassium supplementation in heart failure patients who start spironolactone oral suspension [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 ) and Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] . Check serum potassium levels when ACE inhibitor or ARB therapy is altered in patients receiving spironolactone oral suspension. Examples of drugs that can increase potassium include: ACE inhibitors
rules.actionQuote: Check serum potassium levels when ACE inhibitor or ARB therapy is altered in patients receiving spironolactone oral suspension.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Check serum potassium levels when ACE inhibitor or ARB therapy is altered
rules.summary: Angiotensin receptor blockers can increase potassium and, with spironolactone, may lead to severe hyperkalemia. Check serum potassium when ARB therapy is changed.
rules.quote: Check serum potassium levels when ACE inhibitor or ARB therapy is altered in patients receiving spironolactone oral suspension. Examples of drugs that can increase potassium include: ACE inhibitors angiotensin receptor blockers
rules.actionQuote: Check serum potassium levels when ACE inhibitor or ARB therapy is altered in patients receiving spironolactone oral suspension.

rules.sourceSeverityText: monitor closely to determine if the desired effect of the diuretic is obtained
rules.summary: NSAIDs can reduce the diuretic, natriuretic and antihypertensive effect of spironolactone. When used together, monitor closely to see whether the desired diuretic effect is obtained.
rules.quote: In some patients, the administration of an NSAID can reduce the diuretic, natriuretic, and antihypertensive effect of loop, potassium-sparing, and thiazide diuretics. Therefore, when spironolactone oral suspension and NSAIDs are used concomitantly, monitor closely to determine if the desired effect of the diuretic is obtained
rules.actionQuote: when spironolactone oral suspension and NSAIDs are used concomitantly, monitor closely to determine if the desired effect of the diuretic is obtained

rules.sourceSeverityText: may lead to severe hyperkalemia
rules.summary: NSAIDs are listed among drugs that can increase potassium; with spironolactone this may lead to severe hyperkalemia.
rules.quote: Concomitant administration of spironolactone oral suspension with potassium supplementation or drugs that can increase potassium may lead to severe hyperkalemia. In general, discontinue potassium supplementation in heart failure patients who start spironolactone oral suspension [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 ) and Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] . Check serum potassium levels when ACE inhibitor or ARB therapy is altered in patients receiving spironolactone oral suspension. Examples of drugs that can increase potassium include: ACE inhibitors angiotensin receptor blockers aldosterone blockers non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)

rules.sourceSeverityText: may lead to severe hyperkalemia
rules.summary: Trimethoprim is listed among drugs that can increase potassium; with spironolactone this may lead to severe hyperkalemia.
rules.quote: Concomitant administration of spironolactone oral suspension with potassium supplementation or drugs that can increase potassium may lead to severe hyperkalemia. In general, discontinue potassium supplementation in heart failure patients who start spironolactone oral suspension [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 ) and Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] . Check serum potassium levels when ACE inhibitor or ARB therapy is altered in patients receiving spironolactone oral suspension. Examples of drugs that can increase potassium include: ACE inhibitors angiotensin receptor blockers aldosterone blockers non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) heparin and low molecular weight heparin trimethoprim

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated
rules.summary: Spironolactone is contraindicated in patients with hyperkalemia.
rules.quote: Spironolactone oral suspension is contraindicated for patients with the following conditions: Hyperkalemia

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated
rules.summary: Spironolactone is contraindicated in patients with Addison's disease.
rules.quote: Spironolactone oral suspension is contraindicated for patients with the following conditions: Hyperkalemia Addison’s disease

rules.sourceSeverityText: Monitor potassium closely
rules.summary: Spironolactone is substantially excreted by the kidney; patients with renal impairment are at increased risk of adverse reactions and hyperkalemia. Monitor potassium closely.
rules.quote: Spironolactone oral suspension is substantially excreted by the kidney, and the risk of adverse reactions to this drug may be greater in patients with impaired renal function. Patients with renal impairment are at increased risk of hyperkalemia. Monitor potassium closely.
rules.actionQuote: Monitor potassium closely.

rules.sourceSeverityText: consider initiating treatment at 10 mg (2 mL)
rules.summary: For heart failure treatment in patients with eGFR 30 to 50 mL/min/1.73 m2, consider starting spironolactone oral suspension at 10 mg because of the risk of hyperkalemia.
rules.quote: In patients with an eGFR between 30 and 50 mL/min/1.73m 2 , consider initiating treatment at 10 mg (2 mL) because of the risk of hyperkalemia

rules.sourceSeverityText: initiate spironolactone oral suspension in the hospital ... start with lowest initial dose and titrate slowly
rules.summary: In hepatic disease with cirrhosis and ascites, spironolactone can cause sudden fluid and electrolyte shifts that may precipitate hepatic encephalopathy and coma; start it in hospital. Clearance is reduced in cirrhosis, so start with the lowest initial dose and titrate slowly.
rules.quote: Spironolactone oral suspension can cause sudden alterations of fluid and electrolyte balance which may precipitate impaired neurological function, worsening hepatic encephalopathy and coma in patients with hepatic disease with cirrhosis and ascites. In these patients, initiate spironolactone oral suspension in the hospital [see Dosage and Administration ( 2.4 ), and Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] . Clearance of spironolactone and its metabolites is reduced in patients with cirrhosis. In patients with cirrhosis, start with lowest initial dose and titrate slowly
rules.actionQuote: In patients with cirrhosis, start with lowest initial dose and titrate slowly

rules.sourceSeverityText: avoid spironolactone in pregnant women or advise a pregnant woman of the potential risk to a male fetus
rules.summary: Based on its anti-androgenic properties and animal data, spironolactone may affect sex differentiation of a male fetus. The label says to avoid it in pregnancy or to advise the pregnant woman of the potential risk to a male fetus.
rules.quote: Because of the potential risk to the male fetus due to anti-androgenic properties of spironolactone and animal data, avoid spironolactone in pregnant women or advise a pregnant woman of the potential risk to a male fetus.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding
rules.summary: Spironolactone is not present in breast milk, but its active metabolite canrenone was found in low amounts expected to be clinically inconsequential; long-term infant effects are unknown. Weigh breastfeeding benefits against the mother's need for the drug.
rules.quote: Spironolactone is not present in breastmilk; however, limited data from a lactating woman at 17 days postpartum reports the presence of the active metabolite, canrenone, in human breast milk in low amounts that are expected to be clinically inconsequential. In this case, there were no adverse effects reported for the breastfed infant after short term exposure to spironolactone; however, long term effects on a breastfed infant are unknown. There are no data on spironolactone effects on milk production. Consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding along with the mother’s clinical need for spironolactone and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed child from spironolactone or from the underlying maternal condition.

rules.sourceSeverityText: not recommended for the treatment of hypertension in pediatric patients
rules.summary: Safety and effectiveness in children have not been established. Spironolactone oral suspension is not recommended for treating hypertension in children because of its antiandrogenic, progestogenic and estrogenic properties.
rules.quote: Safety and effectiveness in pediatric patients have not been established. Spironolactone oral suspension is not recommended for the treatment of hypertension in pediatric patients because of the potential risks associated with the antiandrogenic, progestogenic, and estrogenic properties of spironolactone in pediatric patients.

rules.sourceSeverityText: monitor renal function
rules.summary: Because elderly patients are more likely to have decreased renal function, monitor renal function.
rules.quote: Because elderly patients are more likely to have decreased renal function, monitor renal function.
rules.actionQuote: monitor renal function

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with a known hypersensitivity to trimethoprim
rules.summary: Contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to trimethoprim.
rules.quote: Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim is contraindicated in patients with a known hypersensitivity to trimethoprim or sulfonamides, in patients with a history of drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia with use of trimethoprim and/or sulfonamides, and in patients with documented megaloblastic anemia due to folate deficiency.

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with a known hypersensitivity to ... sulfonamides
rules.summary: Contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to sulfonamides.
rules.quote: Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim is contraindicated in patients with a known hypersensitivity to trimethoprim or sulfonamides, in patients with a history of drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia with use of trimethoprim and/or sulfonamides, and in patients with documented megaloblastic anemia due to folate deficiency.

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated
rules.summary: Contraindicated in patients with a history of drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia with use of trimethoprim and/or sulfonamides.
rules.quote: Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim is contraindicated in patients with a known hypersensitivity to trimethoprim or sulfonamides, in patients with a history of drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia with use of trimethoprim and/or sulfonamides, and in patients with documented megaloblastic anemia due to folate deficiency.

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated
rules.summary: Contraindicated in patients with documented megaloblastic anemia due to folate deficiency.
rules.quote: Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim is contraindicated in patients with a known hypersensitivity to trimethoprim or sulfonamides, in patients with a history of drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia with use of trimethoprim and/or sulfonamides, and in patients with documented megaloblastic anemia due to folate deficiency.

rules.sourceSeverityText: also contraindicated in pregnant patients
rules.summary: Contraindicated in pregnancy because sulfonamides cross the placenta and may cause kernicterus.
rules.quote: Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim is also contraindicated in pregnant patients and nursing mothers, because sulfonamides pass the placenta and are excreted in the milk and may cause kernicterus.

rules.sourceSeverityText: also contraindicated in ... nursing mothers
rules.summary: Contraindicated in nursing mothers because sulfonamides are excreted in milk and may cause kernicterus.
rules.quote: Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim is also contraindicated in pregnant patients and nursing mothers, because sulfonamides pass the placenta and are excreted in the milk and may cause kernicterus.

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in pediatric patients less than 2 months of age
rules.summary: Applies only to infants younger than 2 months: the oral suspension is contraindicated.
rules.quote: Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim oral suspension is contraindicated in pediatric patients less than 2 months of age.

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with marked hepatic damage
rules.summary: Contraindicated in patients with marked hepatic damage.
rules.quote: Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim is also contraindicated in patients with marked hepatic damage or with severe renal insufficiency when renal function status cannot be monitored.

rules.sourceSeverityText: should be given with caution to patients with impaired ... hepatic function
rules.summary: Give with caution to patients with impaired hepatic function.
rules.quote: Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim oral suspension should be given with caution to patients with impaired renal or hepatic function, to those with possible folate deficiency (e.g., the elderly, chronic alcoholics, patients receiving anticonvulsant therapy, patients with malabsorption syndrome, and patients in malnutrition states) and to those with severe allergies or bronchial asthma.

rules.sourceSeverityText: should be given with caution to patients with impaired renal ... function
rules.summary: Give with caution to patients with impaired renal function.
rules.quote: Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim oral suspension should be given with caution to patients with impaired renal or hepatic function, to those with possible folate deficiency (e.g., the elderly, chronic alcoholics, patients receiving anticonvulsant therapy, patients with malabsorption syndrome, and patients in malnutrition states) and to those with severe allergies or bronchial asthma.

rules.sourceSeverityText: 1 / 2 the usual regimen
rules.summary: With creatinine clearance 15 to 30 mL/min, use half the usual regimen.
rules.quote: When renal function is impaired, a reduced dosage should be employed using the following table: Creatinine Clearance (mL/min) Recommended Dosage Regimen Above 30 Use standard regimen 15 to 30 1 / 2 the usual regimen

rules.sourceSeverityText: Use not recommended
rules.summary: With creatinine clearance below 15 mL/min, use is not recommended.
rules.quote: 15 to 30 1 / 2 the usual regimen Below 15 Use not recommended

rules.sourceSeverityText: Close monitoring of serum potassium is warranted
rules.summary: Trimethoprim may cause hyperkalemia even at recommended doses in patients with renal insufficiency; close serum potassium monitoring is warranted.
rules.quote: Even treatment with recommended doses may cause hyperkalemia when trimethoprim is administered to patients with underlying disorders of potassium metabolism, with renal insufficiency, or if drugs known to induce hyperkalemia are given concomitantly. Close monitoring of serum potassium is warranted in these patients.

rules.sourceSeverityText: hemolysis may occur
rules.summary: Hemolysis may occur in G6PD-deficient individuals; the reaction is frequently dose-related.
rules.quote: In glucose-6- phosphate dehydrogenase deficient individuals, hemolysis may occur. This reaction is frequently dose-related

rules.sourceSeverityText: should be given with caution ... to those with severe allergies or bronchial asthma
rules.summary: Give with caution to patients with severe allergies or bronchial asthma.
rules.quote: Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim oral suspension should be given with caution to patients with impaired renal or hepatic function, to those with possible folate deficiency (e.g., the elderly, chronic alcoholics, patients receiving anticonvulsant therapy, patients with malabsorption syndrome, and patients in malnutrition states) and to those with severe allergies or bronchial asthma.

rules.sourceSeverityText: should be given with caution ... to those with possible folate deficiency (e.g., ... chronic alcoholics
rules.summary: Give with caution to those with possible folate deficiency, which the label exemplifies with chronic alcoholics.
rules.quote: Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim oral suspension should be given with caution to patients with impaired renal or hepatic function, to those with possible folate deficiency (e.g., the elderly, chronic alcoholics, patients receiving anticonvulsant therapy, patients with malabsorption syndrome, and patients in malnutrition states) and to those with severe allergies or bronchial asthma.

rules.sourceSeverityText: caution is advisable
rules.summary: As with all sulfonamide-containing drugs, caution is advisable in patients with porphyria.
rules.quote: As with all drugs containing sulfonamides, caution is advisable in patients with porphyria or thyroid dysfunction.

rules.sourceSeverityText: caution is advisable
rules.summary: As with all sulfonamide-containing drugs, caution is advisable in patients with thyroid dysfunction.
rules.quote: As with all drugs containing sulfonamides, caution is advisable in patients with porphyria or thyroid dysfunction.

rules.sourceSeverityText: has been reported to be greatly increased
rules.summary: AIDS patients treated for Pneumocystis pneumonia have a greatly increased incidence of side effects (rash, fever, leukopenia, raised transaminases), and hyperkalemia appears more frequent.
rules.quote: The incidence of side effects, particularly rash, fever, leukopenia and elevated aminotransferase (transaminase) values, with sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim therapy in AIDS patients who are being treated for Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia has been reported to be greatly increased compared with the incidence normally associated with the use of sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim in non-AIDS patients. The incidence of hyperkalemia appears to be increased in AIDS patients receiving sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim.

rules.sourceSeverityText: of no significance in phenylketonuric patients on appropriate dietary restriction
rules.summary: Trimethoprim impairs phenylalanine metabolism, but this is of no significance in phenylketonuric patients on appropriate dietary restriction.
rules.quote: Trimethoprim has been noted to impair phenylalanine metabolism, but this is of no significance in phenylketonuric patients on appropriate dietary restriction.

rules.sourceSeverityText: There may be an increased risk of severe adverse reactions in elderly patients
rules.summary: Elderly patients may be at increased risk of severe adverse reactions (skin reactions, bone marrow suppression, low platelets, hyperkalemia), especially with kidney/liver impairment, possible folate deficiency or other drugs.
rules.quote: There may be an increased risk of severe adverse reactions in elderly patients, particularly when complicating conditions exist, e.g., impaired kidney and/or liver function, possible folate deficiency, or concomitant use of other drugs.

rules.sourceSeverityText: the coagulation time should be reassessed
rules.summary: Sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim may prolong the prothrombin time in patients on warfarin; coagulation time should be reassessed.
rules.quote: It has been reported that sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim may prolong the prothrombin time in patients who are receiving the anticoagulant warfarin. This interaction should be kept in mind when sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim is given to patients already on anticoagulant therapy, and the coagulation time should be reassessed.
rules.actionQuote: the coagulation time should be reassessed

rules.sourceSeverityText: thus increasing free methotrexate concentrations
rules.summary: Sulfonamides can displace methotrexate from protein binding and compete with its renal transport, increasing free methotrexate concentrations.
rules.quote: Sulfonamides can also displace methotrexate from plasma protein binding sites and can compete with the renal transport of methotrexate, thus increasing free methotrexate concentrations.

rules.sourceSeverityText: can interfere with a serum methotrexate assay
rules.summary: Trimethoprim can interfere with a serum methotrexate competitive binding protein assay (CBPA) using bacterial dihydrofolate reductase; radioimmunoassay is not affected.
rules.quote: Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim, specifically the trimethoprim component, can interfere with a serum methotrexate assay as determined by the competitive binding protein technique (CBPA) when a bacterial dihydrofolate reductase is used as the binding protein. No interference occurs, however, if methotrexate is measured by a radioimmunoassay (RIA).

rules.sourceSeverityText: Close monitoring of serum potassium is warranted
rules.summary: Trimethoprim may cause hyperkalemia when given with drugs known to induce hyperkalemia, such as ACE inhibitors; close serum potassium monitoring is warranted. Three cases of hyperkalemia in elderly patients have been reported with this combination.
rules.quote: The trimethoprim component of sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim may cause hyperkalemia when administered to patients with underlying disorders of potassium metabolism, with renal insufficiency or when given concomitantly with drugs known to induce hyperkalemia, such as angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors. Close monitoring of serum potassium is warranted in these patients.

rules.sourceSeverityText: potentiates the effect of oral hypoglycemics
rules.summary: Like other sulfonamide-containing drugs, sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim potentiates the effect of oral hypoglycemics.
rules.quote: Like other sulfonamide-containing drugs, sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim potentiates the effect of oral hypoglycemics.

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with: ... Hypersensitivity to tramadol
rules.summary: Contraindicated in patients with hypersensitivity to tramadol (e.g., anaphylaxis).
rules.quote: Hypersensitivity to tramadol (e.g., anaphylaxis)

rules.sourceSeverityText: should not receive
rules.summary: Patients with a history of hypersensitivity reactions to tramadol and other opioids may be at increased risk and should not receive this product.
rules.quote: Patients with a history of hypersensitivity reactions to tramadol and other opioids may be at increased risk and therefore should not receive Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules.

rules.sourceSeverityText: is also contraindicated in patients with
rules.summary: Contraindicated in patients with significant respiratory depression.
rules.quote: Significant respiratory depression [see Warnings and Precautions (5.12) ]

rules.sourceSeverityText: is also contraindicated in patients with
rules.summary: Contraindicated in patients with acute or severe bronchial asthma in an unmonitored setting or in the absence of resuscitative equipment.
rules.quote: Acute or severe bronchial asthma in an unmonitored setting or in the absence of resuscitative equipment

rules.sourceSeverityText: is also contraindicated in patients with
rules.summary: Contraindicated in patients with known or suspected gastrointestinal obstruction, including paralytic ileus.
rules.quote: Known or suspected gastrointestinal obstruction, including paralytic ileus

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated for: All children younger than 12 years of age
rules.summary: Applies to children younger than 12 years only: contraindicated because of life-threatening respiratory depression and death.
rules.quote: Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules are contraindicated for: All children younger than 12 years of age

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated for: ... Postoperative management in children younger than 18 years of age following tonsillectomy and/or adenoidectomy
rules.summary: Contraindicated for postoperative management in children younger than 18 years after tonsillectomy and/or adenoidectomy.
rules.quote: Postoperative management in children younger than 18 years of age following tonsillectomy and/or adenoidectomy

rules.sourceSeverityText: Avoid the use ... in adolescents 12 to 18 years of age who have other risk factors
rules.summary: Applies to adolescents 12 to 18 years with other risk factors for sensitivity to respiratory depression: avoid unless benefits outweigh risks.
rules.quote: Avoid the use of Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules in adolescents 12 to 18 years of age who have other risk factors that may increase their sensitivity to the respiratory depressant effects of tramadol unless the benefits outweigh the risks.

rules.sourceSeverityText: should be used with great caution in patients older than 75 years of age
rules.summary: Use with great caution above 75 years, titrate slowly and frequently reevaluate for CNS and respiratory depression.
rules.quote: For this reason, Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules should be used with great caution in patients older than 75 years of age
rules.actionQuote: Titrate the dosage of Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules slowly in geriatric patients and frequently reevaluate the patient for signs of central nervous system and respiratory depression

rules.sourceSeverityText: advise pregnant women of the potential risk to a fetus
rules.summary: Extended use of opioids in pregnancy may cause neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome; human data are insufficient for birth-defect risk and animal data showed fetal effects, so pregnant women should be advised of the potential fetal risk.
rules.quote: Use of opioid analgesics for an extended period of time during pregnancy may cause neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome [see Warnings and Precautions (5.4) ] . Available data with Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules in pregnant women are insufficient to inform a drug-associated risk for major birth defects and miscarriage.
rules.actionQuote: Based on animal data, advise pregnant women of the potential risk to a fetus.

rules.sourceSeverityText: is not recommended for use in pregnant women during or immediately prior to labor
rules.summary: Not recommended during or immediately before labor, when shorter-acting analgesics or other techniques are more appropriate.
rules.quote: Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules is not recommended for use in pregnant women during or immediately prior to labor, when use of shorter-acting analgesics or other analgesic techniques are more appropriate.

rules.sourceSeverityText: breastfeeding is not recommended
rules.summary: Because of possible excess sedation and respiratory depression in the breastfed infant, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment.
rules.quote: Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, including excess sedation and respiratory depression in a breastfed infant, advise patients that breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules.

rules.sourceSeverityText: should not be used in patients with severe hepatic impairment
rules.summary: The limited ER dose strengths do not allow safe dosing in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C); should not be used.
rules.quote: The limited availability of dose strengths of Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules does not permit the dosing flexibility required for safe use in patients with severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class C). Therefore, Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules should not be used in patients with severe hepatic impairment

rules.sourceSeverityText: has not been studied in patients with hepatic impairment
rules.summary: Metabolism of tramadol and M1 is reduced in advanced cirrhosis; this product has not been studied in hepatic impairment.
rules.quote: Metabolism of tramadol and M1 is reduced in patients with advanced cirrhosis of the liver. Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules has not been studied in patients with hepatic impairment.

rules.sourceSeverityText: should not be used in patients with severe renal impairment
rules.summary: The limited ER dose strengths do not allow safe dosing in severe renal impairment; should not be used.
rules.quote: Therefore, Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules should not be used in patients with severe renal impairment

rules.sourceSeverityText: has not been studied in patients with renal impairment
rules.summary: This product has not been studied in renal impairment; impaired renal function decreases excretion of tramadol and M1.
rules.quote: Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules has not been studied in patients with renal impairment. Impaired renal function results in a decreased rate and extent of excretion of tramadol and its active metabolite, M1.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Risk of seizures may also increase
rules.summary: Seizure risk may increase in patients with epilepsy, a history of seizures, or recognized seizure risk (e.g., head trauma, metabolic disorders, alcohol and drug withdrawal, CNS infections).
rules.quote: Risk of seizures may also increase in patients with epilepsy, those with a history of seizures, or in patients with a recognized risk for seizure (such as head trauma, metabolic disorders, alcohol and drug withdrawal, CNS infections).

rules.sourceSeverityText: Do not prescribe ... for patients who are suicidal
rules.summary: Do not prescribe for patients who are suicidal or addiction-prone; consider non-narcotic analgesics in suicidal or depressed patients.
rules.quote: Do not prescribe Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules for patients who are suicidal or addiction-prone. Consideration should be given to the use of non-narcotic analgesics in patients who are suicidal or depressed

rules.sourceSeverityText: Risks are increased
rules.summary: Risks of addiction, abuse and misuse are increased with a personal or family history of substance abuse or mental illness. (Separately, the label says not to prescribe for addiction-prone patients.)
rules.quote: Risks are increased in patients with a personal or family history of substance abuse (including drug or alcohol abuse or addiction) or mental illness (e.g., major depression).

rules.sourceSeverityText: Prescribe ... with caution
rules.summary: Prescribe with caution for patients with a history of misuse, those taking CNS-active drugs such as tranquilizers or antidepressants, or using alcohol in excess.
rules.quote: Prescribe Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules with caution for patients with a history of misuse and/or who are currently taking CNS-active drugs including tranquilizers or antidepressant drugs, or alcohol in excess, and patients who suffer from emotional disturbance or depression

rules.sourceSeverityText: Regularly evaluate patients
rules.summary: Patients with significant COPD or cor pulmonale, or decreased respiratory reserve, hypoxia, hypercapnia or pre-existing respiratory depression are at increased risk of decreased respiratory drive including apnea; regularly evaluate, especially when initiating and titrating.
rules.quote: Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules treated patients with significant chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or cor pulmonale, and those with a substantially decreased respiratory reserve, hypoxia, hypercapnia, or pre-existing respiratory depression are at increased risk of decreased respiratory drive including apnea, even at recommended dosages of Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules
rules.actionQuote: Regularly evaluate patients, particularly when initiating and titrating Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules and when Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules are given concomitantly with other drugs that depress respiration

rules.sourceSeverityText: Avoid the use
rules.summary: May cause vasodilation that further reduces cardiac output and blood pressure in circulatory shock; avoid.
rules.quote: Avoid the use of Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules in patients with circulatory shock.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Avoid the use
rules.summary: Avoid in patients with impaired consciousness or coma.
rules.quote: Avoid the use of Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules in patients with impaired consciousness or coma.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Monitor such patients for signs of sedation and respiratory depression
rules.summary: In patients with increased intracranial pressure or brain tumors, CO2 retention can further raise intracranial pressure; monitor for sedation and respiratory depression, especially at initiation.
rules.quote: Monitor such patients for signs of sedation and respiratory depression, particularly when initiating therapy with Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Regularly evaluate
rules.summary: Tramadol may cause sphincter of Oddi spasm; regularly evaluate patients with biliary tract disease, including acute pancreatitis, for worsening symptoms.
rules.quote: Regularly evaluate patients with biliary tract disease, including acute pancreatitis, for worsening symptoms.

rules.sourceSeverityText: patients had predisposing risk factors (e.g., diabetes)
rules.summary: Tramadol-associated hypoglycemia has been reported, mostly in patients with predisposing risk factors such as diabetes; if suspected, monitor blood glucose.
rules.quote: Cases of tramadol-associated hypoglycemia have been reported, some resulting in hospitalization. In most cases, patients had predisposing risk factors (e.g., diabetes).
rules.actionQuote: If hypoglycemia is suspected, monitor blood glucose levels and consider drug discontinuation as appropriate

rules.sourceSeverityText: should not use
rules.summary: CYP2D6 ultra-rapid metabolizers form M1 more rapidly and may have life-threatening respiratory depression even at labeled doses; they should not use this product.
rules.quote: Therefore, individuals who are ultra-rapid metabolizers should not use Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules.

rules.sourceSeverityText: frequently evaluate the patient
rules.summary: Concomitant SSRIs can cause serotonin syndrome; if use is warranted, frequently evaluate the patient, especially at initiation and dose changes, and stop tramadol if serotonin syndrome is suspected.
rules.quote: Serotonergic Drugs Clinical Impact: The concomitant use of opioids with other drugs that affect the serotonergic neurotransmitter system has resulted in serotonin syndrome [see Warnings and Precautions (5.9) ]. Intervention: If concomitant use is warranted, frequently evaluate the patient, particularly during treatment initiation and dose adjustment. Discontinue Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules if serotonin syndrome is suspected. Examples: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs)

rules.sourceSeverityText: frequently evaluate the patient
rules.summary: Concomitant serotonergic drugs can cause serotonin syndrome; if use is warranted, frequently evaluate the patient and stop tramadol if serotonin syndrome is suspected.
rules.quote: Serotonergic Drugs Clinical Impact: The concomitant use of opioids with other drugs that affect the serotonergic neurotransmitter system has resulted in serotonin syndrome [see Warnings and Precautions (5.9) ]. Intervention: If concomitant use is warranted, frequently evaluate the patient, particularly during treatment initiation and dose adjustment. Discontinue Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules if serotonin syndrome is suspected. Examples: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs)

rules.sourceSeverityText: increases the seizure risk
rules.summary: Concomitant use of tramadol increases seizure risk in patients taking SSRIs.
rules.quote: Concomitant use of tramadol increases the seizure risk in patients taking: [see Drug Interactions (7) ] Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) antidepressants or anorectics, Tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), and other tricyclic compounds (e.g., cyclobenzaprine, promethazine, etc.), Other opioids

rules.sourceSeverityText: reserve concomitant prescribing of these drugs for use in patients for whom alternative treatment options are inadequate
rules.summary: Concomitant use with other opioids (CNS depressants) may cause profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma and death; reserve co-prescribing for patients without adequate alternatives and use the lowest doses and shortest durations.
rules.quote: Profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death may result from the concomitant use of Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules with benzodiazepines and/or other CNS depressants, including alcohol (e.g., non-benzodiazepine sedatives/hypnotics, anxiolytics, tranquilizers, muscle relaxants, general anesthetics, antipsychotics, gabapentinoids [gabapentin and pregabalin], and other opioids). Because of these risks, reserve concomitant prescribing of these drugs for use in patients for whom alternative treatment options are inadequate.

rules.sourceSeverityText: increases the seizure risk
rules.summary: Concomitant use of tramadol increases seizure risk in patients taking other opioids.
rules.quote: Concomitant use of tramadol increases the seizure risk in patients taking: [see Drug Interactions (7) ] Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) antidepressants or anorectics, Tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), and other tricyclic compounds (e.g., cyclobenzaprine, promethazine, etc.), Other opioids

rules.sourceSeverityText: Evaluate patients ... at frequent intervals
rules.summary: CYP3A4 inhibitors such as macrolide antibiotics may increase tramadol levels, raising risk of seizures, serotonin syndrome and fatal respiratory depression; evaluate patients at frequent intervals.
rules.quote: The concomitant use of Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules with cytochrome P450 3A4 inhibitors, such as macrolide antibiotics (e.g., erythromycin), azole-antifungal agents (e.g., ketoconazole), and protease inhibitors (e.g., ritonavir) or discontinuation of a cytochrome P450 3A4 inducer such as rifampin, carbamazepine, and phenytoin, may result in an increase in tramadol plasma concentrations, which could increase or prolong adverse reactions, increase the risk for serious adverse events including seizures and serotonin syndrome, and may cause potentially fatal respiratory depression.
rules.actionQuote: Evaluate patients receiving Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules and any CYP3A4 inhibitor or inducer at frequent intervals for the risk for serious adverse events including seizures and serotonin syndrome, signs and symptoms that may reflect opioid toxicity and opioid withdrawal when Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules is used in conjunction with inhibitors and inducers of CYP3A4

rules.sourceSeverityText: Evaluate patients ... at frequent intervals
rules.summary: CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase tramadol levels, raising risk of seizures, serotonin syndrome and fatal respiratory depression; evaluate patients at frequent intervals.
rules.quote: The concomitant use of Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules with cytochrome P450 3A4 inhibitors, such as macrolide antibiotics (e.g., erythromycin), azole-antifungal agents (e.g., ketoconazole), and protease inhibitors (e.g., ritonavir) or discontinuation of a cytochrome P450 3A4 inducer such as rifampin, carbamazepine, and phenytoin, may result in an increase in tramadol plasma concentrations, which could increase or prolong adverse reactions, increase the risk for serious adverse events including seizures and serotonin syndrome, and may cause potentially fatal respiratory depression.
rules.actionQuote: Evaluate patients receiving Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules and any CYP3A4 inhibitor or inducer at frequent intervals for the risk for serious adverse events including seizures and serotonin syndrome, signs and symptoms that may reflect opioid toxicity and opioid withdrawal when Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules is used in conjunction with inhibitors and inducers of CYP3A4

rules.sourceSeverityText: Frequently reevaluate the prothrombin time
rules.summary: Rare postmarketing reports of altered warfarin effect including raised prothrombin time; frequently reevaluate prothrombin time and adjust warfarin as needed.
rules.quote: Warfarin Clinical Impact: Post-marketing surveillance of tramadol has revealed rare reports of alteration of warfarin effect, including elevation of prothrombin times. Intervention: Frequently reevaluate the prothrombin time of patients on warfarin for signs of an interaction and adjust the dosage of warfarin as needed.

rules.sourceSeverityText: evaluate patients at frequent intervals
rules.summary: CYP2D6 inhibitors can raise tramadol levels and lower M1 levels, which can increase the risk of seizures and serotonin syndrome or cause opioid withdrawal. Evaluate patients at frequent intervals.
rules.quote: Inhibitors of CYP2D6 Clinical Impact: The concomitant use of Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules and CYP2D6 inhibitors may result in an increase in the plasma concentration of tramadol and a decrease in the plasma concentration of M1, particularly when an inhibitor is added after a stable dose of Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules is achieved.
rules.actionQuote: If concomitant use of a CYP2D6 inhibitor is necessary, evaluate patients at frequent intervals for adverse reactions including opioid withdrawal, seizures, and serotonin syndrome.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Evaluate patients ... at frequent intervals
rules.summary: CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase tramadol levels, raising risk of seizures, serotonin syndrome and fatal respiratory depression; evaluate patients at frequent intervals.
rules.quote: The concomitant use of Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules with cytochrome P450 3A4 inhibitors, such as macrolide antibiotics (e.g., erythromycin), azole-antifungal agents (e.g., ketoconazole), and protease inhibitors (e.g., ritonavir) or discontinuation of a cytochrome P450 3A4 inducer such as rifampin, carbamazepine, and phenytoin, may result in an increase in tramadol plasma concentrations, which could increase or prolong adverse reactions, increase the risk for serious adverse events including seizures and serotonin syndrome, and may cause potentially fatal respiratory depression.
rules.actionQuote: Evaluate patients receiving Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules and any CYP3A4 inhibitor or inducer at frequent intervals for the risk for serious adverse events including seizures and serotonin syndrome, signs and symptoms that may reflect opioid toxicity and opioid withdrawal when Tramadol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules is used in conjunction with inhibitors and inducers of CYP3A4

rules.sourceSeverityText: Evaluate patients for signs of diminished diuresis and/or effects on blood pressure
rules.summary: Opioids can reduce the effect of diuretics. Evaluate for reduced urine output and blood pressure effects, and increase the diuretic dose as needed.
rules.quote: Diuretics Clinical Impact: Opioids can reduce the efficacy of diuretics by inducing the release of antidiuretic hormone. Intervention: Evaluate patients for signs of diminished diuresis and/or effects on blood pressure and increase the dosage of the diuretic as needed.
rules.actionQuote: Evaluate patients for signs of diminished diuresis and/or effects on blood pressure and increase the dosage of the diuretic as needed.

rules.sourceSeverityText: closely monitor patients receiving any such drug with warfarin
rules.summary: Ibuprofen is listed among NSAIDs that can increase the risk of bleeding with warfarin; the label says to closely monitor patients receiving such drugs with warfarin.
rules.quote: Nonsteroidal Anti-Inflammatory Agents celecoxib, diclofenac, diflunisal, fenoprofen, ibuprofen, indomethacin, ketoprofen, ketorolac, mefenamic acid, naproxen, oxaprozin, piroxicam, sulindac
rules.actionQuote: Because bleeding risk is increased when these drugs are used concomitantly with warfarin, closely monitor patients receiving any such drug with warfarin.

rules.sourceSeverityText: closely monitor patients receiving any such drug with warfarin

rules.quote: Nonsteroidal Anti-Inflammatory Agents celecoxib, diclofenac, diflunisal, fenoprofen, ibuprofen, indomethacin, ketoprofen, ketorolac, mefenamic acid, naproxen, oxaprozin, piroxicam, sulindac
rules.actionQuote: Because bleeding risk is increased when these drugs are used concomitantly with warfarin, closely monitor patients receiving any such drug with warfarin.

rules.sourceSeverityText: closely monitor patients receiving any such drug with warfarin
rules.summary: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agents are listed as a drug class that can increase the risk of bleeding with warfarin; closely monitor patients receiving such drugs with warfarin.
rules.quote: Nonsteroidal Anti-Inflammatory Agents celecoxib, diclofenac, diflunisal, fenoprofen, ibuprofen, indomethacin, ketoprofen, ketorolac, mefenamic acid, naproxen, oxaprozin, piroxicam, sulindac
rules.actionQuote: Because bleeding risk is increased when these drugs are used concomitantly with warfarin, closely monitor patients receiving any such drug with warfarin.

rules.sourceSeverityText: closely monitor patients receiving any such drug with warfarin
rules.summary: Clopidogrel is listed among antiplatelet agents that can increase the risk of bleeding with warfarin; closely monitor patients receiving such drugs with warfarin.
rules.quote: Antiplatelet Agents aspirin, cilostazol, clopidogrel, dipyridamole, prasugrel, ticlopidine
rules.actionQuote: Because bleeding risk is increased when these drugs are used concomitantly with warfarin, closely monitor patients receiving any such drug with warfarin.

rules.sourceSeverityText: closely monitor patients receiving any such drug with warfarin

rules.quote: Antiplatelet Agents aspirin, cilostazol, clopidogrel, dipyridamole, prasugrel, ticlopidine
rules.actionQuote: Because bleeding risk is increased when these drugs are used concomitantly with warfarin, closely monitor patients receiving any such drug with warfarin.

rules.sourceSeverityText: closely monitor patients receiving any such drug with warfarin
rules.summary: Other anticoagulants are listed as a drug class that can increase the risk of bleeding with warfarin; closely monitor patients receiving such drugs with warfarin.
rules.quote: Anticoagulants argatroban, dabigatran, bivalirudin, desirudin, heparin, lepirudin
rules.actionQuote: Because bleeding risk is increased when these drugs are used concomitantly with warfarin, closely monitor patients receiving any such drug with warfarin.

rules.sourceSeverityText: closely monitor patients receiving any such drug with warfarin
rules.summary: Sertraline is listed among serotonin reuptake inhibitors that can increase the risk of bleeding with warfarin; closely monitor patients receiving such drugs with warfarin.
rules.quote: Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors citalopram, desvenlafaxine, duloxetine, escitalopram, fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, milnacipran, paroxetine, sertraline, venlafaxine, vilazodone
rules.actionQuote: Because bleeding risk is increased when these drugs are used concomitantly with warfarin, closely monitor patients receiving any such drug with warfarin.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Closely monitor INR
rules.summary: Ciprofloxacin is listed as an example CYP1A2 inhibitor; such inhibitors have the potential to increase the effect (increase INR) of warfarin. The label says to closely monitor INR.
rules.quote: CYP1A2 acyclovir, allopurinol, caffeine, cimetidine, ciprofloxacin
rules.actionQuote: Closely monitor INR if a concomitant drug is a CYP2C9, 1A2, and/or 3A4 inhibitor or inducer.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Closely monitor INR
rules.summary: Clarithromycin is listed as an example CYP3A4 inhibitor; such inhibitors have the potential to increase the effect (increase INR) of warfarin. The label says to closely monitor INR.
rules.quote: CYP3A4 alprazolam, amiodarone, amlodipine, amprenavir, aprepitant, atorvastatin, atazanavir, bicalutamide, cilostazol, cimetidine, ciprofloxacin, clarithromycin
rules.actionQuote: Closely monitor INR if a concomitant drug is a CYP2C9, 1A2, and/or 3A4 inhibitor or inducer.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Closely monitor INR
rules.summary: Amlodipine is listed as an example CYP3A4 inhibitor; such inhibitors have the potential to increase the effect (increase INR) of warfarin. The label says to closely monitor INR.
rules.quote: CYP3A4 alprazolam, amiodarone, amlodipine
rules.actionQuote: Closely monitor INR if a concomitant drug is a CYP2C9, 1A2, and/or 3A4 inhibitor or inducer.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Closely monitor INR

rules.quote: CYP3A4 alprazolam, amiodarone, amlodipine, amprenavir, aprepitant, atorvastatin
rules.actionQuote: Closely monitor INR if a concomitant drug is a CYP2C9, 1A2, and/or 3A4 inhibitor or inducer.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Closely monitor INR
rules.summary: Omeprazole is listed in Table 2 as an example CYP1A2 inducer; inducers have the potential to decrease the effect (decrease INR) of warfarin. The label says to closely monitor INR.
rules.quote: zileuton montelukast, moricizine, omeprazole, phenobarbital, phenytoin, cigarette smoking
rules.actionQuote: Closely monitor INR if a concomitant drug is a CYP2C9, 1A2, and/or 3A4 inhibitor or inducer.

rules.sourceSeverityText: More frequent INR monitoring should be performed when starting or stopping botanicals
rules.summary: St. John's wort is named as a botanical that may decrease the effects of warfarin and may interact through CYP450. More frequent INR monitoring is advised when starting or stopping botanicals.
rules.quote: Conversely, some botanicals may decrease the effects of warfarin sodium (e.g., co-enzyme Q 10 , St. John's wort, ginseng).
rules.actionQuote: More frequent INR monitoring should be performed when starting or stopping botanicals.

rules.sourceSeverityText: may be responsible for decreased INR response
rules.summary: Increased vitamin K intake may be responsible for a decreased INR response to warfarin.
rules.quote: The following factors may be responsible for decreased INR response: increased vitamin K intake or hereditary warfarin resistance.

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in women who are pregnant
rules.summary: Warfarin is contraindicated in pregnancy, except in pregnant women with mechanical heart valves who are at high risk of thromboembolism.
rules.quote: Warfarin sodium tablets, USP are contraindicated in women who are pregnant except in pregnant women with mechanical heart valves, who are at high risk of thromboembolism

rules.sourceSeverityText: Monitor breastfeeding infants for bruising or bleeding
rules.summary: Breastfed infants of mothers taking warfarin should be monitored for bruising or bleeding.
rules.quote: Clinical Considerations Monitor breastfeeding infants for bruising or bleeding.
rules.actionQuote: Monitor breastfeeding infants for bruising or bleeding.

rules.sourceSeverityText: monitor their INR more frequently
rules.summary: No dose adjustment is needed in renal impairment, but patients with renal impairment should monitor INR more frequently.
rules.quote: No dosage adjustment is necessary for patients with renal impairment. Instruct patients with renal impairment taking warfarin to monitor their INR more frequently
rules.actionQuote: Instruct patients with renal impairment taking warfarin to monitor their INR more frequently

rules.sourceSeverityText: Conduct more frequent monitoring for bleeding
rules.summary: Hepatic impairment can potentiate the response to warfarin; monitor more frequently for bleeding.
rules.quote: Hepatic impairment can potentiate the response to warfarin through impaired synthesis of clotting factors and decreased metabolism of warfarin. Conduct more frequent monitoring for bleeding when using warfarin sodium in these patients.
rules.actionQuote: Conduct more frequent monitoring for bleeding when using warfarin sodium in these patients.

rules.sourceSeverityText: the risks of warfarin sodium therapy may be increased
rules.summary: In moderate to severe hepatic impairment the risks of warfarin therapy may be increased.
rules.quote: In the following clinical settings, the risks of warfarin sodium therapy may be increased: • Moderate to severe hepatic impairment

rules.sourceSeverityText: Conduct more frequent monitoring for bleeding
rules.summary: In elderly patients, monitor more frequently for bleeding in any situation or physical condition where added risk of hemorrhage is present.
rules.quote: Conduct more frequent monitoring for bleeding with administration of warfarin sodium to elderly patients in any situation or with any physical condition where added risk of hemorrhage is present.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Consider lower initiation and maintenance doses
rules.summary: The label says to consider lower initiation and maintenance doses of warfarin in elderly patients.
rules.quote: Consider lower initiation and maintenance doses of warfarin sodium in elderly patients

rules.sourceSeverityText: Risk factors for bleeding include
rules.summary: Age 65 or older is listed as a risk factor for bleeding on warfarin.
rules.quote: Risk factors for bleeding include high intensity of anticoagulation (INR >4.0), age greater than or equal to 65, history of highly variable INRs, history of gastrointestinal bleeding, hypertension, cerebrovascular disease, anemia, malignancy, trauma, renal impairment, certain genetic factors

rules.sourceSeverityText: more frequent INR determinations are recommended
rules.summary: Target INR ranges may be hard to achieve and maintain in pediatric patients, and more frequent INR determinations are recommended.
rules.quote: target INR ranges may be difficult to achieve and maintain in pediatric patients, and more frequent INR determinations are recommended.

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with
rules.summary: Warfarin is contraindicated in patients with hemorrhagic tendencies or blood dyscrasias.
rules.quote: Warfarin sodium tablets, USP are contraindicated in patients with: • Hemorrhagic tendencies or blood dyscrasias

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with
rules.summary: Warfarin is contraindicated with bleeding tendencies associated with active ulceration or overt bleeding of the GI, genitourinary or respiratory tract, or CNS hemorrhage.
rules.quote: Bleeding tendencies associated with: o Active ulceration or overt bleeding of the gastrointestinal, genitourinary, or respiratory tract o Central nervous system hemorrhage

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with
rules.summary: Warfarin is contraindicated with bleeding tendencies associated with cerebral aneurysms or dissecting aorta.
rules.quote: o Cerebral aneurysms, dissecting aorta

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with
rules.summary: Warfarin is contraindicated with bleeding tendencies associated with pericarditis and pericardial effusions.
rules.quote: o Pericarditis and pericardial effusions

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with
rules.summary: Warfarin is contraindicated with bleeding tendencies associated with bacterial endocarditis.
rules.quote: o Bacterial endocarditis

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with
rules.summary: Warfarin is contraindicated with recent or contemplated surgery of the CNS or eye, or traumatic surgery resulting in large open surfaces.
rules.quote: Recent or contemplated surgery of the central nervous system or eye, or traumatic surgery resulting in large open surfaces

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with
rules.summary: Warfarin is contraindicated in threatened abortion, eclampsia and preeclampsia.
rules.quote: Threatened abortion, eclampsia, and preeclampsia

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with
rules.summary: Warfarin is contraindicated in unsupervised patients with conditions associated with a potential high level of non-compliance.
rules.quote: Unsupervised patients with conditions associated with potential high level of non-compliance

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in any unsupervised patient with senility
rules.summary: Warfarin is contraindicated in any unsupervised patient with senility.
rules.quote: Warfarin sodium is contraindicated in any unsupervised patient with senility.

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with
rules.summary: Warfarin is contraindicated with spinal puncture and other diagnostic or therapeutic procedures with potential for uncontrollable bleeding.
rules.quote: Spinal puncture and other diagnostic or therapeutic procedures with potential for uncontrollable bleeding

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with
rules.summary: Warfarin is contraindicated with major regional or lumbar block anesthesia.
rules.quote: Major regional or lumbar block anesthesia

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with
rules.summary: Warfarin is contraindicated in malignant hypertension.
rules.quote: Malignant hypertension

rules.sourceSeverityText: Do not use warfarin sodium as initial therapy
rules.summary: Warfarin should not be used as initial therapy in patients with HIT or HITTS; it may be considered after the platelet count has normalized.
rules.quote: Do not use warfarin sodium as initial therapy in patients with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) and with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia with thrombosis syndrome (HITTS).
rules.actionQuote: Treatment with warfarin sodium may be considered after the platelet count has normalized.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Risk factors for bleeding include
rules.summary: A history of gastrointestinal bleeding is listed as a risk factor for bleeding on warfarin.
rules.quote: Risk factors for bleeding include high intensity of anticoagulation (INR >4.0), age greater than or equal to 65, history of highly variable INRs, history of gastrointestinal bleeding, hypertension, cerebrovascular disease, anemia, malignancy, trauma, renal impairment, certain genetic factors

rules.sourceSeverityText: Risk factors for bleeding include
rules.summary: Hypertension is listed as a risk factor for bleeding on warfarin.
rules.quote: Risk factors for bleeding include high intensity of anticoagulation (INR >4.0), age greater than or equal to 65, history of highly variable INRs, history of gastrointestinal bleeding, hypertension, cerebrovascular disease, anemia, malignancy, trauma, renal impairment, certain genetic factors

rules.sourceSeverityText: the risks of warfarin sodium therapy may be increased
rules.summary: Diabetes mellitus is listed among clinical settings in which the risks of warfarin therapy may be increased.
rules.quote: • Polycythemia vera • Vasculitis • Diabetes mellitus

rules.sourceSeverityText: contraindicated in patients with
rules.summary: Warfarin is contraindicated in patients with hypersensitivity to warfarin or any other component of the product (e.g., anaphylaxis).
rules.quote: Hypersensitivity to warfarin or to any other components of this product (e.g., anaphylaxis)

rules.sourceSeverityText: Closely monitor INR
rules.summary: Changes in INR have been reported in patients taking warfarin with antibiotics. Closely monitor INR when starting or stopping any antibiotic.
rules.quote: There have been reports of changes in INR in patients taking warfarin and antibiotics or antifungals, but clinical pharmacokinetic studies have not shown consistent effects of these agents on plasma concentrations of warfarin. Closely monitor INR when starting or stopping any antibiotic or antifungal in patients taking warfarin.
rules.actionQuote: Closely monitor INR when starting or stopping any antibiotic or antifungal in patients taking warfarin.

rules.sourceSeverityText: can weaken the effects of many medicines, including crucially important medicines
rules.summary: St. John's wort can weaken the effects of many medicines, and warfarin is listed among the crucially important ones.
rules.quote: For example, St. John’s wort can weaken the effects of many medicines, including crucially important medicines such as: Some antidepressants, including amitriptyline and bupropion Birth control pills Cyclosporine, which prevents the body from rejecting transplanted organs Some drugs used to prevent seizures, including phenytoin and carbamazepine Some heart medications, including digoxin and ivabradine Some HIV drugs, including indinavir and nevirapine Some cancer medications, including irinotecan, imatinib, and docetaxel Warfarin, an anticoagulant (blood thinner)
rules.actionQuote: If you take any type of medicine, talk with your health care provider before using St. John’s wort or other herbal products; some herbs and medicines interact in harmful ways.

rules.sourceSeverityText: Calcium supplements may interact with medications

rules.sourceSeverityText: can potentially reduce iron absorption

rules.sourceSeverityText: experts recommend taking calcium and iron supplements at different times

rules.quote: Potassium-sparing diuretics, such as amiloride (Midamor) and spironolactone (Aldactone), reduce the excretion of potassium in the urine and can cause hyperkalemia [77,78]. rules.sourceSeverityText: even dietary potassium intakes below the AI can cause hyperkalemia

rules.sourceSeverityText: serious and potentially dangerous interaction; need to maintain a consistent intake of vitamin K
rules.summary: Vitamin K can interact seriously with warfarin, which works against vitamin K. People taking warfarin need to keep their vitamin K intake from food and supplements consistent, because sudden changes can raise or lower the anticoagulant effect.
rules.quote: Vitamin K can have a serious and potentially dangerous interaction with anticoagulants such as warfarin (Coumadin) as well as phenprocoumon, acenocoumarol, and tioclomarol, which are commonly used in some European countries [7,8]. These drugs antagonize the activity of vitamin K, leading to the depletion of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors. People taking warfarin and similar anticoagulants need to maintain a consistent intake of vitamin K from food and supplements because sudden changes in vitamin K intakes can increase or decrease the anticoagulant effect [45].
rules.actionQuote: People taking warfarin and similar anticoagulants need to maintain a consistent intake of vitamin K from food and supplements

rules.sourceSeverityText: might be more pronounced with cephalosporin antibiotics
rules.summary: This is about the medicine affecting vitamin K, not the other way round. Antibiotics can lower vitamin K status by killing gut bacteria that make it, and this may be more pronounced with cephalosporins, which might also inhibit vitamin K action. Vitamin K supplements are usually not needed unless antibiotic use is prolonged and vitamin K intake is poor.
rules.quote: Antibiotics can destroy vitamin K-producing bacteria in the gut, potentially decreasing vitamin K status. This effect might be more pronounced with cephalosporin antibiotics, such as cefoperazone (Cefobid), because these antibiotics might also inhibit the action of vitamin K in the body [6,46]. Vitamin K supplements are usually not needed unless antibiotic use is prolonged (beyond several weeks) and accompanied by poor vitamin K intake [46].
